# Jimmy Essex: A Comprehensive Biographical Study of a Modern British Performer
## 1\. Introduction: The Archetype of the Versatile British Artist
The contemporary landscape of the British performing arts industry is a complex ecosystem that demands a high degree of adaptability from its participants. Unlike the studio systems of the mid-20th century, which often pigeonholed actors into specific genres or mediums, the modern era requires a fluidity of skill that transcends the traditional boundaries between musical theatre, serial television drama, commercial dance, and independent cinema. Jimmy Essex stands as a quintessential example of this 21st-century archetype. His career, spanning over two decades, offers a fascinating case study in professional longevity, artistic reinvention, and the navigation of public visibility in the digital age.

Born in the mid-1980s and emerging from the rigorous training grounds of the Guildford School of Acting (GSA), Essex’s trajectory has not been linear. Instead, it has been characterized by a series of strategic pivots that have allowed him to remain relevant in an industry notorious for its volatility. From the high-octane, ephemeral world of reality television and commercial pop music to the grinding, fast-paced production schedules of national soap operas, and finally to the intimate, psychologically demanding sphere of fringe theatre, Essex has cultivated a diverse portfolio that defies easy categorization.

To understand Essex’s career is to understand the changing mechanics of British fame and artistic credibility. His early work as a backup dancer for global icons like Janet Jackson and Lady Gaga highlights the often-overlooked physicality and discipline required of ensemble performers. His tenure on *The X Factor* with the group MITSOTU serves as a lens through which to view the "manufactured" pop machine of the early 2010s. His most recognized role, as Adam Donovan in *Hollyoaks*, provides a substantial body of work for analyzing the cultural function of the soap opera "heartthrob" and the narrative possibilities of long-form serial storytelling.

Furthermore, Essex’s recent work in the 2020s—specifically his transition into challenging stage roles addressing themes of chemsex and political polarization, alongside appearances in prestige streaming series like Netflix’s *The Sandman*—signals a mature phase of artistic engagement. This report aims to provide an exhaustive, unparalleled examination of Jimmy Essex’s life and work. It will dissect his training, analyze the critical reception of his key roles, explore the socio-cultural context of his projects, and evaluate his impact as an openly gay actor and advocate within the LGBTQ+ community. Through this detailed chronicle, we gain insight not only into the man himself but into the broader currents of the British entertainment industry in the first quarter of the 21st century.

## 2\. Early Life, Geography, and Professional Formation
### 2.1 Geographic Roots and Identity
Jimmy Essex was born in 1984 (or possibly late 1983/early 1985 depending on specific academic year alignments) . His background is deeply rooted in the cultural duality of the Southeast of England. While some sources link his birth to Coventry, his surname and much of his formative public identity are inextricably tied to the county of Essex and the Greater London borough of Harrow .

This geographic distinction is not merely trivial; in the context of British performance, "Essex" and "London" carry distinct socio-cultural signifiers. The "Essex" identity in British media often connotes a specific type of working-class authenticity, approachability, and a "cheeky" charisma—traits that would later be heavily utilized in the marketing of his *Hollyoaks* character. Conversely, his connection to Harrow and the broader London performance scene aligns him with the cosmopolitan, trained rigor of the capital’s artistic elite. This blend of grounded relatability and metropolitan sophistication has been a hallmark of his public persona, allowing him to appeal to broad television audiences while credible in the sophisticated circles of West End theatre.

### 2.2 Foundational Training: Soul Performing Arts
Before entering the hallowed halls of conservatory training, Essex honed his craft at **Soul Performing Arts** in Ruislip . Local performing arts schools play a critical role in the British talent pipeline, serving as the first filter for identifying youth with genuine potential. It was here that Essex likely developed the fundamental discipline required for dance—a medium that demands physical conditioning comparable to elite athletics.

During these formative years, he met future collaborators, including James Collins, with whom he would later form the band MITSOTU. The bonds formed in these early training environments are often enduring, creating a network of peers that supports a performer throughout their career. The curriculum at such institutions typically emphasizes a "triple threat" approach—acting, singing, and dancing—which prepares students for the multifaceted demands of the commercial industry.

### 2.3 The Guildford School of Acting (GSA)
Essex’s acceptance into and graduation from the **Guildford School of Acting (GSA)** in 2005 marked his transition from an aspiring amateur to a credentialed professional . GSA is widely recognized as one of the premier drama schools in the United Kingdom, particularly renowned for its Musical Theatre program.

#### 2.3.1 The GSA Pedagogy and Impact
Training at GSA is notoriously rigorous. The institution traces its lineage back to the mid-20th century and has produced a staggering list of alumni who dominate the West End and British television. For Essex, graduating in 2005 placed him in a cohort entering the industry at a time of significant change, where the divide between "serious" acting and "musical theatre" was beginning to blur, yet still posed challenges for casting directors.

The GSA curriculum focuses heavily on:

* **Vocal Technique:** Ensuring longevity and stamina, which Essex would later rely on during his music career and stage runs. 
* **Physical Acting:** The school is known for producing actors who are physically expressive. This is evident in Essex’s later reviews, which often cite his ability to use "stillness" and body language to convey subtext . 
* **Professional Preparation:** GSA is noted for its industry showcases, which likely facilitated Essex's early entry into commercial dance and agent representation.

Graduating in the mid-2000s, Essex entered a competitive marketplace. His training equipped him with a technical toolkit that allowed him to survive the "gig economy" nature of the performing arts—booking commercials, dance contracts, and ensemble work while awaiting a breakthrough role.

## 3\. The Commercial Dance and Music Era (2005–2015)
The decade following his graduation was defined by high-energy performance work. This period is crucial for understanding Essex’s work ethic and his understanding of spectacle. Unlike actors who move straight into repertory theatre, Essex cut his teeth in the commercial sector, where the emphasis is on precision, image, and the ability to deliver under the glare of arena lights.

### 3.1 The World of Commercial Dance
Essex found significant success as a professional dancer, a career path that is often undervalued in biographical accounts of actors but is essential for developing stage presence.

#### 3.1.1 Collaborations with Global Icons
Essex’s resume includes work with some of the most demanding figures in the music industry:

* **Janet Jackson:** Known for her intricate, synchronized choreography, Jackson’s tours are a pinnacle for commercial dancers. Securing a spot in her troupe indicates an elite level of dance proficiency . 
* **Lady Gaga:** Essex appeared in the music video for "Alejandro" (2010) . This video, directed by Steven Klein, is a piece of high-concept visual art characterized by sharp, militaristic choreography and a dark, cabaret aesthetic. Participating in such a project exposed Essex to the intersection of avant-garde fashion, music, and performance art.

The discipline required for these roles—rehearsing for 12 hours a day, maintaining peak physical fitness, and executing choreography with robotic precision—instilled in Essex a professionalism that would later be noted by his television colleagues. It also gave him a comfort level with large-scale production environments, ensuring that he would not be intimidated by the machinery of television sets or film soundstages.

### 3.2 The X Factor and MITSOTU (2012)
In 2011/2012, Essex pivoted from backing dancer to frontman, forming the group **MITSOTU** (Music Is The Soul Of The Universe) with his childhood friend James Collins and vocalist Holly Cooper .

#### 3.2.1 The Concept of "Urban Pop"
The trio marketed themselves as an "urban pop" act. In the context of 2012 British music, this was a strategic attempt to ride the wave of popularity enjoyed by artists like Rihanna, N-Dubz, and the burgeoning UK grime/pop crossover scene. However, MITSOTU distinguished themselves by emphasizing their status as a "band" rather than a manufactured vocal group. They wrote their own material and toured local schools to build a grassroots following before approaching the televised talent machinery .

#### 3.2.2 The X Factor Journey (Series 9\)
The group auditioned for *The X Factor* in 2012, a year when the show was still a cultural juggernaut in the UK, commanding millions of viewers and dominating the tabloid discourse.

* **The Audition:** They performed in front of a reported live audience of 6,000 people—a daunting prospect for any performer. Their performance secured four "yes" votes from the judges (Gary Barlow, Tulisa, Louis Walsh, and guest judge Mel B/Geri Halliwell depending on the specific city leg), validating their commercial potential . 
* **The Branding:** The group displayed a high level of commitment, with all three members getting "MITSOTU" tattoos on their left arms . This level of branding suggests a serious intent to succeed as a unit, rather than just a casual attempt at fame. 
* **The Outcome:** The group progressed through "Bootcamp," a grueling selection process in Liverpool where hundreds of acts were cut . They reached the "Judges' Houses" stage (or the final cut before it), mentored by Louis Walsh. Ultimately, they did not reach the live finals .

While the group did not achieve superstardom, the exposure was invaluable. It placed Essex on national television, introducing his face to casting directors and the general public. It also demonstrated his vocal ability, proving he was more than just a dancer. The "failure" to advance can often be a blessing in disguise for actors, as it avoids the "reality TV stigma" that can sometimes hamper a transition into serious dramatic roles. Essex emerged with his credibility intact, known as a talented performer rather than a reality show caricature.

### 3.3 Other Commercial Ventures
During this period, Essex also appeared in high-profile advertising campaigns. Notably, he was the face of a **Euro Cup Coca-Cola advert**.9 Commercial acting requires a specific skill set: the ability to convey a narrative or emotion in mere seconds, often without dialogue. This work contributed to his financial stability and kept him active in front of the camera between larger projects.

## 4\. The Hollyoaks Era: Soap Opera Stardom (2016–2018)
In 2016, Essex secured the role that would define the next phase of his career: Adam Donovan in the Channel 4 soap opera *Hollyoaks*. This casting was a significant breakthrough, moving him from the periphery of the entertainment world to its center.

### 4.1 The Institution of *Hollyoaks*
To understand the significance of this role, one must understand the specific place *Hollyoaks* occupies in British culture. Unlike its older counterparts *Coronation Street* or *EastEnders*, which focus on working-class community realism, *Hollyoaks* is targeted at a younger demographic. It is known for its stylized aesthetic, high-concept storylines, and a cast composed largely of young, attractive actors. It serves as a proving ground for new talent, with alumni often moving on to Hollywood or prime-time drama.

### 4.2 The "Donovan Brothers" Strategy
Essex’s casting was part of a major strategic overhaul of the show's cast. In early 2016, producers announced the arrival of the "Donovan Brothers"—Adam, Liam (Maxim Baldry), and Jesse (Luke Jerdy)—as new regular characters .

* **The Archetype:** The brothers were introduced as "cheeky," "bold," and "brazen" heartthrobs, designed to fill the void left by departing male leads . They were half-brothers to the established villain Grace Black (Tamara Wall), instantly connecting them to the show's central power dynamics. 
* **Adam Donovan’s Characterisation:** Within the trio, Adam was the eldest and the most complex. While his brothers were initially portrayed as carefree playboys, Adam was written with a "strong conscience" . He was the "responsible" brother, the one who "wouldn't stray over the line." This initial setup was crucial, as it provided the baseline from which his character would eventually fall.

### 4.3 Narrative Arcs and Character Psychology
Essex’s tenure on the show was marked by several high-profile storylines that utilized the soap opera format to explore themes of loyalty, betrayal, and toxic masculinity.

#### 4.3.1 Romantic Melodrama
A staple of the genre is the romantic triangle, and Adam Donovan was central to one of the show’s most prominent ones during 2016–2017. He was engaged to Maxine Minniver (Nikki Sanderson), a long-standing character beloved by fans. The relationship was destabilized by the arrival of Darcy Wilde, Adam’s "dead" ex-fiancée who returned to wreak havoc. 
Essex’s performance in these scenes required him to balance romantic idealism with gullibility. He had to make the audience believe that Adam—a smart, capable man—could be manipulated by Darcy’s machinations. Critics and fans engaged heavily with this plot, often expressing frustration with Adam’s choices, a testament to Essex’s ability to evoke an emotional response from the viewership.

#### 4.3.2 The "Backstabber" and the Criminal Descent
The defining arc of Adam Donovan’s existence was his relationship with his father, Glenn Donovan (Bob Cryer). As the storylines progressed into 2017 and 2018, the show began to deconstruct the "good brother" image.

* **Moral Corruption:** Adam was slowly drawn into his father’s criminal empire. This was not a sudden heel-turn but a gradual erosion of his morals, driven by a misplaced desire for paternal approval and family unity. 
* **The "Cards of Fate":** In a highly stylized marketing campaign for the show's "flash-forward" week, Adam was associated with the "Backstabber" tarot card . This foreshadowed his dual role: appearing to be a loyal soldier for his father while secretly working as a police informant to bring him down. 
* **Acting Challenge:** This period required Essex to play a "double role"—Adam the criminal and Adam the informant. He had to convey the immense stress of living a lie, adding a layer of gritty realism to the often heightened world of *Hollyoaks*.

### 4.4 The Exit: A Tragic Filicide
Essex’s departure from the show in May 2018 was executed with a level of finality rare in soap operas, where characters often leave in taxis to allow for future returns.

* \*\* The Scene:\*\* In a shocking climax, Glenn Donovan discovered Adam’s betrayal and shot him dead . 
* **Significance:** The act of filicide (a father killing his son) is a heavy narrative device with Shakespearean undertones. It cemented Glenn’s status as a true villain and provided Adam with a tragic redemption arc. 
* **Essex’s Reflection:** In exit interviews, Essex expressed satisfaction with the conclusion. He noted, "I like the build-up to it – a good guy gone bad and then it turns back round, but then it's too late" . He recognized that a definitive death made the story more impactful than a quiet exit.

### 4.5 Critical Recognition and Impact
Essex’s work on *Hollyoaks* was well-regarded by the industry.

* **Awards:** He received a nomination for **Best Drama Star** at the Inside Soap Awards and was involved in the **Best Exit** conversations . These nominations are voted on by viewers and panels, indicating both popularity and critical respect. 
* **Legacy:** The Donovan era is remembered by fans as a strong period for the show, with Essex’s Adam serving as the moral anchor of a chaotic family unit.

## 5\. Theatrical Evolution: Challenging Norms (2019–2025)
Leaving a high-profile TV role carries risks. Many soap actors struggle to find work or are typecast. Essex, however, actively sought out roles that would deconstruct his "soap hunk" image, turning to the London stage to tackle gritty, politically charged material.

### 5.1 *GHBoy* (2020): Exploring Trauma and Chemsex
In late 2020, Essex starred in the world premiere of **GHBoy** at the Charing Cross Theatre .

* **The Subject Matter:** The play deals with the phenomenon of "chemsex" (the use of drugs like GHB in sexual contexts) within the gay community. It is a harrowing, controversial topic that is often stigmatized or ignored in mainstream media. 
* **The Role:** Essex played Robert, a man grappling with the psychological aftermath of these experiences. The role required immense vulnerability, demanding that Essex portray dissociation, trauma, and the desperate search for connection. 
* **Critical Intent:** In interviews, Essex stated his desire to tell queer stories that moved beyond the "coming out" narrative . He wanted to explore the darker, more complex realities of LGBTQ+ life in London. This choice demonstrated a commitment to using his platform to shed light on difficult community issues.

### 5.2 *Happy Ending* (2025): Political Polarization and Intimacy
In the autumn of 2025, Essex returned to the stage in **Happy Ending**, written and directed by Ronnie Larsen, at the Waterloo East Theatre .

#### 5.2.1 The Two-Hander Dynamic
The play is a "two-hander"—a piece of theatre featuring only two actors—which places maximum pressure on the performers to sustain the audience's attention. Essex played **Andrew** (or Andy), a gay massage therapist, opposite Billy Walker’s **Mr. Miller**, a MAGA-supporting client .

#### 5.2.2 Themes and Performance
The play used the intimate, confined setting of a massage room to explore the macroscopic political divides of the Western world.

* **Character:** Essex’s Andrew was described by critics as "softly spoken," "uptight," and "meticulous" . This characterization is a significant departure from the confident, swaggering Adam Donovan. 
* **Technique:** Reviews highlighted Essex’s mastery of non-verbal communication. One critic noted his "expressive facial reactions behind his client's back" and the effectiveness of his "stillness" during the other character’s monologues . 
* **Reception:** The play received 4-star reviews, with critics praising the "intense chemistry" between Essex and Walker . It was lauded as a "provocative comedy-thriller" that managed to be both funny and emotionally weighty .

This production solidified Essex’s reputation as a serious stage actor capable of handling nuanced, dialogue-heavy scripts that blend comedy with social commentary.

## 6\. Expansion into Prestige Streaming and Film (2022–2025)
Parallel to his theatre work, Essex successfully broke into the international streaming market, a notoriously difficult transition for British soap actors.

### 6.1 Netflix’s *The Sandman* (2022)
Essex was cast in the Netflix adaptation of Neil Gaiman’s *The Sandman*, one of the most expensive and anticipated series of 2022\.

* **Production Scale:** Shot on 8K Red Monstro cameras with a massive budget, *The Sandman* represented the pinnacle of high-end television production . 
* **The Role:** Essex played **Carrion** in the episode "Collectors" . The episode depicts a convention of serial killers, a dark and disturbing concept from the graphic novels. 
* **Significance:** While a supporting role, being part of the "Sandman Universe" (DC Comics) placed Essex on a global stage. It demonstrated his ability to fit into genre storytelling (fantasy/horror) and work alongside a cast that included A-list talent like David Thewlis and Stephen Fry.

### 6.2 *EastEnders* (2025)
In November 2025, Essex returned to the BBC to take a guest role in *EastEnders* as a character named **Rich**.1

* **Context:** *EastEnders* is the BBC's flagship soap. Even a guest appearance is a marker of status within the British acting fraternity. 
* **The Role:** Appearing on 13 November 2025, the role of Rich allowed Essex to dip back into the soap world without the commitment of a long-term contract, keeping his profile high among domestic audiences .

### 6.3 Independent Film
Essex has continued to build his film reel with independent projects:

* ***A Dark Path*** **(2020/2023):** A horror/thriller in which he played Peter . 
* ***Daddy Issues*** **(2025):** A short film where he played Felix . 
* Read In For Me (2024): A short film role as Joe . 
 These projects allow him to experiment with different directors and styles, free from the constraints of network television.

## 7\. Entrepreneurship, Advocacy, and Personal Life
Beyond his roles, Essex has cultivated a public identity centered on education, advocacy, and authenticity.

### 7.1 Beyond Performing Arts
In 2018, Essex co-founded **Beyond Performing Arts** with Francesca Lyons .

* **The Venture:** A performing arts school aimed at children and young adults. 
* **Philosophy:** Essex serves as a teacher and choreographer, using his real-world experience to guide the next generation. His bio for the school emphasizes creating a "safe and fun environment" . This venture reflects a desire to give back to the community and provides a stable career pillar alongside the fluctuating nature of acting work.

### 7.2 LGBTQ+ Advocacy and *Trailblazers*
Essex is openly gay and has used his platform to advocate for LGBTQ+ rights and visibility.

* **The Relationship:** He has been in a relationship with musician **Charles Simmons** since 2013 . The couple’s journey has been documented on social media, from their engagement (c. 2019\) to their marriage . By sharing his life openly, Essex challenges the old industry norm where leading men were encouraged to stay in the closet to protect their "heartthrob" status. 
* ***Trailblazers*** **(2019):** Essex participated in this travel series, which saw queer creatives visiting European cities to explore local LGBTQ+ history and culture . As a presenter, he discussed the nuances of traveling as a gay couple, contributing to the normalization of queer relationships in lifestyle programming.

To provide a comprehensive reference, the following tables detail Essex’s known work across various mediums.

## 9\. Critical Assessment and Legacy
### 9.1 The "Triple Threat" in Practice
Essex represents the efficacy of the "triple threat" training model. His career is not defined by a single skill but by the ability to deploy different skills as the market demands. When reality TV was the dominant cultural force (2012), he utilized his singing and pop sensibility. When soaps needed fresh energy (2016), he utilized his acting and screen charisma. When the theatre world demanded gritty realism (2020s), he utilized his dramatic training.

### 9.2 Subverting the "Soap Hunk" Trope
While initially cast in *Hollyoaks* to fulfill a visual archetype—the handsome, charming brother—Essex consistently worked to deepen the portrayal. His post-soap choices are particularly revealing. Instead of pursuing similar "heartthrob" roles or reality TV competition shows (like *I'm a Celebrity...*), he chose *GHBoy* and *Happy Ending*—plays that deconstruct sexuality and masculinity. This suggests an artist who is deeply interested in the psychology of the modern man, particularly the modern gay man, and is willing to risk his commercial appeal to explore it.

### 9.3 Conclusion
As of late 2025, Jimmy Essex stands as a mature, multifaceted artist. He has successfully navigated the perilous waters of early fame, reality TV, and soap opera stardom to emerge as a respected stage actor and entrepreneur. His journey from the dance studios of Ruislip to the sets of Netflix blockbusters serves as an inspiring blueprint for aspiring performers, proving that longevity in the entertainment industry is built not just on talent, but on resilience, adaptability, and the courage to constantly reinvent oneself.

Jimmy Essex was involved in the Best Exit conversations at the Inside Soap Awards.
In late 2020, Jimmy Essex starred in the world premiere of GHBoy at the Charing Cross Theatre.
The play GHBoy deals with the phenomenon of "chemsex" (the use of drugs like GHB in sexual contexts) within the gay community.
Chemsex is a harrowing, controversial topic that is often stigmatized or ignored in mainstream media.
Jimmy Essex played Robert in GHBoy, a man grappling with the psychological aftermath of chemsex experiences.
The role of Robert in GHBoy required immense vulnerability, demanding that Jimmy Essex portray dissociation, trauma, and the desperate search for connection.
In interviews, Jimmy Essex stated his desire to tell queer stories that moved beyond the "coming out" narrative.
In the autumn of 2025, Jimmy Essex returned to the stage in Happy Ending, which was written and directed by Ronnie Larsen, at the Waterloo East Theatre.
Happy Ending is a "two-hander"—a piece of theatre featuring only two actors—which places maximum pressure on the performers to sustain the audience's attention.
Jimmy Essex played Andrew (or Andy), a gay massage therapist, opposite Billy Walker’s Mr. Miller, a MAGA-supporting client in Happy Ending.
Jimmy Essex's character Andrew in Happy Ending was described by critics as "softly spoken," "uptight," and "meticulous".
Reviews highlighted Jimmy Essex’s mastery of non-verbal communication in Happy Ending.
One critic noted Jimmy Essex's "expressive facial reactions behind his client's back" and the effectiveness of his "stillness" during the other character’s monologues in Happy Ending.
The play Happy Ending received 4-star reviews.
Critics praised the "intense chemistry" between Jimmy Essex and Billy Walker in Happy Ending.
Happy Ending was lauded as a "provocative comedy-thriller" that managed to be both funny and emotionally weighty.
Jimmy Essex was cast in the Netflix adaptation of Neil Gaiman’s The Sandman.
The Sandman was one of the most expensive and anticipated series of 2022.
The Sandman was shot on 8K Red Monstro cameras with a massive budget.
Jimmy Essex played Carrion in The Sandman episode "Collectors".
The episode "Collectors" depicts a convention of serial killers, a dark and disturbing concept from the graphic novels.
Being part of the "Sandman Universe" (DC Comics) placed Jimmy Essex on a global stage.
Jimmy Essex's role in The Sandman demonstrated his ability to fit into genre storytelling (fantasy/horror) and work alongside a cast that included A-list talent like David Thewlis and Stephen Fry.
In November 2025, Jimmy Essex returned to the BBC to take a guest role in EastEnders as a character named Rich.
EastEnders is the BBC's flagship soap.
Even a guest appearance on EastEnders is a marker of status within the British acting fraternity.
Appearing on 13 November 2025, the role of Rich allowed Jimmy Essex to dip back into the soap world without the commitment of a long-term contract, keeping his profile high among domestic audiences.
Jimmy Essex has continued to build his film reel with independent projects.
Jimmy Essex played Peter in the horror/thriller feature film A Dark Path (2020/2023).
Jimmy Essex played Felix in the short film Daddy Issues (2025).
Jimmy Essex had a role as Joe in the short film Read In For Me (2024).
In 2018, Jimmy Essex co-founded Beyond Performing Arts with Francesca Lyons.
Beyond Performing Arts is a performing arts school aimed at children and young adults.
Jimmy Essex serves as a teacher and choreographer at Beyond Performing Arts, using his real-world experience to guide the next generation.
Jimmy Essex's bio for Beyond Performing Arts emphasizes creating a "safe and fun environment".
Jimmy Essex is openly gay and has used his platform to advocate for LGBTQ+ rights and visibility.
Jimmy Essex has been in a relationship with musician Charles Simmons since 2013.
The couple’s journey (Jimmy Essex and Charles Simmons) has been documented on social media, from their engagement (c. 2019) to their marriage.
By sharing his life openly, Jimmy Essex challenges the old industry norm where leading men were encouraged to stay in the closet to protect their "heartthrob" status.
Jimmy Essex participated in the travel series Trailblazers (2019).
Trailblazers saw queer creatives visiting European cities to explore local LGBTQ+ history and culture.
As a presenter on Trailblazers, Jimmy Essex discussed the nuances of traveling as a gay couple, contributing to the normalization of queer relationships in lifestyle programming.
Jimmy Essex was a contestant as part of the group MITSOTU on The X Factor (Series 9) in 2012, reaching Judges' Houses/Bootcamp.
Jimmy Essex played Adam Donovan in Hollyoaks from 2016–2018 as a Series Regular, involved in the "Backstabber" storyline.
Jimmy Essex appeared as himself in the travel documentary series Trailblazers in 2019.
Jimmy Essex played Carrion in The Sandman, Season 1, Episode 9 ("Collectors") in 2022.
Jimmy Essex had a guest appearance as Rich in EastEnders on 13 Nov 2025.
Jimmy Essex played Peter in the feature film A Dark Path (Horror/Thriller genre) in 2020/2023.
Jimmy Essex played Joe in the short film Read In For Me, directed by Štefánia Lovasová, in 2024.
Jimmy Essex played Felix in the short film Daddy Issues, directed by Misha Vertkin, in 2025.
Jimmy Essex played Robert in the production GHBoy at the Charing Cross Theatre in 2020.
Jimmy Essex played Andrew in the production Happy Ending at the Waterloo East Theatre in 2025, directed by Ronnie Larsen.
Jimmy Essex was a dancer for Lady Gaga's "Alejandro" music video in 2010.
Jimmy Essex was a male dancer for Mr Bowler Presents' "Hideaway" music video in 2014.
Jimmy Essex was the Lead/Face for a Coca-Cola Euro Cup Advert.
As of late 2025, Jimmy Essex stands as a mature, multifaceted artist.

Happy Ending at Waterloo East Theatre Review
============================================

[Reviews](https://theatreandtonic.co.uk/blog/category/Reviews)

1 Oct

Written By [Emmie Newitt](https://theatreandtonic.co.uk/blog?author=63734d746ff51f59aef838be)

![Image 4: Two men are talking near a massage table](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/63734f8309e2800b55c9fc71/f1b7b068-c005-4b01-9566-be8b807f09d6/happy+ending+waterloo+east+review)

Billy Walker and Jimmy Essex. Photo by Gareth McLeod

**Written by Penny****for Theatre & Tonic**

**Disclaimer: Gifted tickets in exchange for an honest review**

**Suitable for audiences aged 18+. This production contains some strong language and nudity.**

* * *

Producer **Adam Roebuck** (**_F**king Men_**) has brought this new play written by **Ronnie Larsen** to the intimate space of the Waterloo East Theatre for a limited run. **_Happy Ending_** is set in a massage studio, in which Andy, a gay massage therapist has his routine disturbed by the arrival of a new client, Mr. Miller, a straight Trump supporter. But is everything as it first appears?

The set is simple, clean and a little impersonal. There’s a massage table in the centre, a couple of plants, pristine white towels and no personal touches. This is a good reflection of the personality that therapist Andy displays – he is 100% a professional, keeping his personal life completely separate from work.

Larsen’s script is very well structured. On first impressions, it appears that the story will be about a Trump supporting bigot learning to be a bit more tolerant and empathetic. As Mr Miller arrives for his appointment he is a typical Alpha male, clearly uncomfortable and asserting his masculinity in everything from his comments about women to his choice of background music. The clues are there from the start that there is more to this two-hander (pun not intended) than meets the eye. As Miller slowly opens up about his marriage, the peer pressure that has led to him voting for Trump and even his taste in music, barriers begin to come down and there’s a developing shift in the relationship between therapist and client and some clear similarities between the two men that flies in the face of their surface differences.

Larsen also directs and his choices clearly bring out every nuance in his script. The way the characters move around the stage suggests a game of “cat and mouse”, with the massage table, an essential part of the therapist/client professional transaction, acting as both a defensive barrier and a neutral territory as the two men’s interactions evolve. Initially the dialogue is slightly gabbled, but as the play progresses Larsen introduces pauses that add to both the tension and the growing understanding between these two men. There’s plenty of humour in the script and the staging of intimacy is very well handled – it never becomes smutty or uncomfortable.

**Jimmy Essex** and **Billy Walker** are well cast as Andy and Mr Miller. There is an instant chemistry between the characters and they easily convey their characters’ discomfort with their initial interactions. As Andy, Essex is softly spoken and a little uptight, his concern for his professional reputation always at the forefront of his mind. But he clearly reveals his inner feelings with expressive facial reactions behind his client’s back. His stillness during a monologue from Mr Miller was very effective, serving to amplify the words being spoken through his attentiveness.

Walker’s all American MAGA fan was a fish out of water in the massage room. Although swagger and bravado kicked in, a sense of vulnerability was always there in his portrayal. He also has great comic timing that really comes out with the excellent music choices that accompany the action, whether he’s getting down to classic American rock or serving a flamboyant lip sync to Adele!

As the play reaches its conclusion, audience perceptions of both men will have changed. Having bared all, both physically and emotionally, we’ve found out so much more about their characters than first impressions suggested. A few minutes could possibly be shaved off the running time as quite a lot of the early interaction is spent establishing the obvious differences between the men. This said, it’s a very entertaining hour and a bit (running at just over 70 minutes at this performance), and leaves you hoping for a “happy ending”, however you wish to interpret that phrase!

**Happy Ending runs at the Waterloo East Theatre until Sunday 26th October. Find out more and book tickets**[**here**](https://www.waterlooeast.co.uk/happy-ending)**.**

★★★★

2.content:
[![Image 1: This is a good article. Click here for more information.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/94/Symbol_support_vote.svg/20px-Symbol_support_vote.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Good_articles* "This is a good article. Click here for more information.")

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

| Jimmy Essex |
| --- |
| Occupations | Actor Musician Dancer |
| Years active | 2011– |
| Television | _[The X Factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_X\_Factor\_(British\_TV\_series) "The X Factor (British TV series)")_ _[Hollyoaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollyoaks "Hollyoaks")_ |
| Spouse | Charles Simmons |

**Jimmy Essex** is a British actor, dancer and musician. Essex performed as part of a band in the [ninth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_X_Factor_(British_TV_series)_series_9 "The X Factor (British TV series) series 9") of _[The X Factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_X\_Factor\_(British\_TV\_series) "The X Factor (British TV series)")_ in 2012, but the band did not get through to the live finals. Essex has also worked as a [backup dancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backup_dancer "Backup dancer"). From 2016 to 2018, Essex played the regular role of [Adam Donovan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Donovan_(Hollyoaks) "Adam Donovan (Hollyoaks)") on the British [soap opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soap_opera "Soap opera")_[Hollyoaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollyoaks "Hollyoaks")_. Essex played the lead role in the 2020 play _GHBoy_ and has appeared in other acting projects.

Essex was born in 1984 or 1985.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_4-3) He is from [Harrow, London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrow,_London "Harrow, London").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-X_Factor_1-4) Essex is a singer and actor and has been in the [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre "West End theatre").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-5) In 2014, Essex appeared in the video _Mr Bowler Presents - Hideaway_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Credits-6) He has also been a [backup dancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backup_dancer "Backup dancer") for [Janet Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Jackson "Janet Jackson").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-X_Factor_1-4) In 2012, Essex appeared in the [ninth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_X_Factor_(British_TV_series)_series_9 "The X Factor (British TV series) series 9") of the British television music competition _[The X Factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_X\_Factor\_(British\_TV\_series) "The X Factor (British TV series)")_, performing as part of the band "MITSOTU" (which stands for "Music Is The Soul Of The Universe") with James Collins and Holly Cooper.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-X_Factor_1-4)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-X_Factor_2-7) The group, who had previously performed in various London schools in 2011, did their first audition for the show in June 2012 in front of an audience of 6000 people and went through to the next stage of the show after scoring four "yes" votes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-X_Factor_1-4) All three members had "MITSOTU" tattooed on their left arms.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-X_Factor_1-4) The group was unsuccessful in getting to the talent show's live finals, losing out to rival group MK1.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-X_Factor_2-7) However, the band continued performing gigs at other venues, such as [Kensington Roof Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kensington_Roof_Gardens "Kensington Roof Gardens").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-X_Factor_2-7) Reflecting on the experience in 2017, Essex said, "It was such a fun time in my life and I did it with my two best friends, so I wouldn't have changed it. But I am glad that it ended where it did, because it's left the door open for other things and I think if it had gone any further, it probably would have stopped that from happening."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Darcy-8) He added that he still likes to sing but could not imagine singing in public anymore.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Darcy-8) Essex was also in the 2016 advertisements for [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coca-Cola "Coca-Cola"), which he filmed in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-9)

Essex enjoyed working with Lisa Maxwell (_pictured_) on _Hollyoaks_

In March 2016, it was announced that Essex joined the cast of the British soap opera _[Hollyoaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollyoaks "Hollyoaks")_ as [Adam Donovan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Donovan_(Hollyoaks) "Adam Donovan (Hollyoaks)"), who was introduced with his younger brothers [Jesse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Donovan "Jesse Donovan") ([Luke Jerdy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Jerdy "Luke Jerdy")) and [Liam Donovan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Donovan "Liam Donovan") ([Maxim Baldry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxim_Baldry "Maxim Baldry")) as an extension of [Grace Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grace_Black "Grace Black")'s ([Tamara Wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamara_Wall "Tamara Wall")) family.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_1-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-11) Essex was thrilled to join the soap, saying, "_Hollyoaks_ is already starting to feel like home. Adam has some amazing storylines coming up and I can't wait to share them with the fans. The Donovan brothers are definitely going to cause a stir!"[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_1-10) Essex, Baldry and Jerdy had auditioned together.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-12) Essex' debut as Adam aired in April of that year.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_4-3)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_1-10) After his initial appearance in April 2016,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_1-10) Essex's return to the soap aired on 13 June of that year.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-13) Essex revealed that he felt very nervous when he first started on the soap, and Jerdy said that Essex was so nervous saying his lines during his first scenes that he was shaking, although he "got away with it" because it was cold.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_3-14)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_4-3) Essex later said that he became more comfortable working on the soap.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_4-3) Jerdy and Wall have joked that Essex was the "worst" for giggling on set and would sometimes have to walk off set because of it.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-16) Essex felt like that the Donovan brothers had been received positively by _Hollyoaks_ viewers.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Darcy-8) The actor had been a fan of _Hollyoaks_ and felt nervous meeting some of the cast as he knew them from watching the show.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Interview_2-17) Essex also enjoyed working with [Lisa Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_Maxwell_(actress) "Lisa Maxwell (actress)"), who plays the brothers' mother [Tracey Donovan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracey_Donovan "Tracey Donovan"), and found it "bizarre" to work with her initially as he used to watch her on television, and Essex ended up getting to know her and went to her house.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Darcy-8)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Interview-18) As his character was a [hairdresser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hairdresser "Hairdresser"), Essex was given some lessons in the profession to help him with the portrayal.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Interview-18)

> "I was so nervous, that I spent about a week learning [my lines] through and through. It was awful. I forgot how to walk. I was walking same arms and legs because I was that nervous. It was horrible".

–Essex reflecting on his initial _Hollyoaks_ scenes (2018)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_4-3)

One of Adam's storyline saw a love triangle between Adam, [Maxine Minniver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxine_Minniver "Maxine Minniver") ([Nikki Sanderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Sanderson "Nikki Sanderson")) and [Darcy Wilde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darcy_Wilde "Darcy Wilde") ([Aisling Jarrett-Gavin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aisling_Jarrett-Gavin "Aisling Jarrett-Gavin")).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-19)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Darcy-8) Essex wanted Maxine and Adam to get married as he described himself a "sucker for a wedding".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-20) Essex enjoyed working with Jarrett-Gavin and revealed that the pair would spend time together out outside of work, adding that the pair got along "like a house on fire".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Darcy-8) Essex and Jarrett-Gavin had also gone to the same school.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-21) In 2018, Adam was involved in a storyline where his behaviour got darker and was involved in a mystery storyline where Adam was seen being told to shoot someone in a flash forward episode; Essex enjoyed portraying the villainous side to the character, but believed that Adam was doing bad things for the "right reasons in his mind".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-24) The plot eventually led to Adam being fatally shot by his father [Glenn Donovan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Donovan "Glenn Donovan") (Bob Cryer) in the episode originally airing on 23 May 2018, which shocked and upset _Hollyoaks_ viewers.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_2-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-27) Reflecting on his departure in a video on _Hollyoaks'_[YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") channel, Essex thanked the _Hollyoaks_ team and viewers for supporting him.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_3-14)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_2-26) Essex brought in doughnuts on his last day working on the soap.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_3-14) He also described his _Hollyoaks_ experience as "the best two and a half years ever".[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_3-14) Essex also said that he was very happy with his exit storyline, saying, "I think it's really, really shocking. I like the build-up to it - the good guy gone bad and then it turns back round, but then it's too late".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_4-3) He also liked how it made Glenn's character "so evil".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Hollyoaks_4-3)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-28) Adam's death was longlisted for "Best Exit" at the [2018 _Inside Soap_ Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside_Soap_Awards#2018 "Inside Soap Awards").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-30) Sanderson revealed in 2019 that she still kept in touch with Essex and enjoyed working with him.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-31)

Essex portrayed Peter in the 2020 film _A Dark Path_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Credits-6)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-32) Essex was then part of the cast of the play _GHBoy_, which was due to be performed in December 2020 at [Charing Cross Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charing_Cross_Theatre "Charing Cross Theatre").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-GHBoy-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Chemsex-34) The play explored [chemsex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemsex "Chemsex") within the LGBTQ+ male community.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Chemsex-34) Essex portrayed Robert Finch, a character who is grieving the death of his father whilst dealing with substance abuse and infidelity.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Chemsex-34)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-GHBoy-33) Essex said that the character's "innocence" and "vulnerability" drew him into the role, and said that he related to the character's "journey", adding, "I've made choices based on things that I've wanted, and not maybe looked at who that may be hurting".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Chemsex-34) Essex was happy to have the "challenge" of theatre, and said that he wanted to tell [LGBTQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ "LGBTQ") stories beyond the "coming out thing".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Chemsex-34) Essex also expressed frustration at the lack of support given by the government towards the theatre industry during the [COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_Kingdom "COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom"), saying, "I think [the arts have] been quite neglected, it's really been pushed aside and treated as a second-class job".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Chemsex-34) In 2025, Essex was part of the short film _Daddy Issues_.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Daddy_Issues-35)

Essex had a dog named Stevie as of 2017.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Interview-18)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-36) Whilst working on _Hollyoaks_, Essex would often visit his colleagues [Jessica Ellis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Ellis "Jessica Ellis") ([Tegan Lomax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegan_Lomax "Tegan Lomax")) and [Andrew Hayden-Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Hayden-Smith "Andrew Hayden-Smith") ([DS Gavin Armstrong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DS_Gavin_Armstrong "DS Gavin Armstrong")) with Stevie.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-37) Essex said that he and Ellis were good friends and that Ellis took him under her wing went he started working on the soap, and commented that they both like watching "rubbish TV" and documentaries.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Interview-18) Essex has also described himself as a big "fantasy buff".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Interview-18) Essex is also friends with fellow soap opera actor [Jonny Labey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonny_Labey "Jonny Labey").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Interview_2-17) Essex has revealed that he often gets asked if he is related to [Joey Essex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joey_Essex "Joey Essex"), which he is not.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Darcy-8) In October 2017, Essex worked with his _Hollyoaks_ colleagues Jarrett-Gavin, Maxwell and Wall to raise money for the charity [Centrepoint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centrepoint_(charity) "Centrepoint (charity)") as part of its Sleep Out event in Manchester, with the event including the actress and Essex reading a bedtime story.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-39) Essex said in 2017 that his favourite actor is [James McAvoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_McAvoy "James McAvoy").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Interview-18)

Essex is part of the [LGBTQ+ community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ%2B_community "LGBTQ+ community").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-LGBTQ+-40) Essex began dating musician Charles Simmons in 2013.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-43)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-LGBTQ+-40) Essex revealed in January 2019 that the couple had gotten engaged after Simmons had proposed to him with a diamond ring whilst the pair were on holiday in [Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lanka "Sri Lanka").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-46) Essex' former _Hollyoaks_ co-stars congratulated him on the news.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-47) Later in 2019, Essex and Simmons were featured in an episode of _Trailblazers_, an LGBTQ+ video [miniseries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miniseries "Miniseries") created by _[Gay Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay\_Times "Gay Times")_ and [Celebrity Cruises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Cruises "Celebrity Cruises").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-LGBTQ+-40)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-48) Essex and Simmons discussed their love of food in one of the episodes, with Essex joking, "At breakfast we plan what we're going to have for lunch, and at lunch we plan what we're going to have for dinner".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-LGBTQ+-40) In 2020, it was reported that Essex and Simmons were married.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Essex#cite_note-Chemsex-34)

9.title: About Us – Beyond Performing Arts
9.content:
**Beyond** offers an experience **like no other** with industry **professional teachers** delivering **first hand insight** into the **world of performing arts**…

Beyond Performing Arts
----------------------

**Beyond Performing Arts** is an **innovative** and **exciting** new **performing arts schoo**l founded by **Jimmy Essex** and **Francesca Lyons** in 2018.

**Beyond** offers an experience like no other with **industry professional teachers** delivering first hand insight into the **world of performing arts**.

Teachers credits include **Hollyoaks, X-Factor, Britain’s got Talent**, and various **international cruise ships** to name a few! As well as regular classes, **Beyond** offers **West End/TV acting****workshops** throughout the year led by cast members of the West end’s leading shows and some of the biggest names in television.

Since opening, the school has seen a great amount of success and word of mouth spread fast about the fun, high energy and **current** classes Beyond has to offer.

Classes start from ages 4 and above in acting, singing and dancing and all levels are welcome.

If you haven’t already heard enough, **Francesca** and **Jimmy** invite you for a **free trial day** where you can come and experience all **Beyond** has to offer for yourself.

Meet Our amazing

Dance Teachers
--------------------------------

#### Francesca **Lyons**

**Singing, Dance and Musical Theatre Teacher**

Francesca found her passion for singing and performing at a young age and met Jimmy at 14 where they trained at a theatre school together until they auditioned for professional college. Francesca trained for 3 years at the prestigious Urdang Academy where she trained extensively in acting, dancing and singing. After leaving, Francesca worked nonstop as a vocalist and went from contract to contract on various cruise ships as vocalist and a dancer.

Francesca has sung a very vast range of styles and studied vocally how to approach different ways of singing. Francesca has worked in the recording studio too and is a front singer for the cover band Penthouse 5.

Francesca trained over the years in The Estill model and studied anatomy of the voice and how to break down and teach various vocal styles. Francesca studied how to work with adolescent voices and it is her pleasure to coach and teach children how to sing safely yet gain confidence to explore and push their voices (safely) beyond their inhibitions and insecurities.

#### Jimmy **Essex**

**Acting & Dance Teacher / Choreographer**

Jimmy has already had a long and rich career in all areas of the performing arts industry. After completing training at The Urdang Academy in London, he jumped straight into professional dancing, appearing in shows like The X factor and Britain’s Got Talent.

He has toured with major UK artists including The Saturdays and even performed at Capital FM’s winter and summer time balls. More recently, Jimmy appeared in the hit channel 4 show Hollyoaks where he played Adam Donovan for 2 years. He was also the face of the Euro cup Coca Cola advert. Bringing all of his experiences to teaching, Jimmy adds true insight into the professional world of performing arts.

Jimmy has a true passion for creating a safe and fun environment for kids to learn and grow in the industry he loves so much.

11.title: Meet the Donovans! Hollyoaks introduces three new hunks as Grace Black's brothers arrive
11.description: The three newbies are Grace Black's brothers.
11.content:
It's official - _Hollyoaks_ is bringing in Grace Black's three half-brothers as new regulars for the show.

**Digital Spy** can exclusively reveal that Essex boys Liam, Adam and Jesse Donovan will soon be introduced to the Channel 4 soap - providing a new injection of infectious energy as they quickly make their mark on the village.

Middle brother Liam will be the first Donovan to arrive, but his younger sibling Jesse and older bro Adam will be hot on his heels.

Liam, played by Maxim Baldry, makes his first appearance next week when he's admitted as a patient at Dee Valley Hospital. While there, he quickly catches the eye of both Tegan Lomax and Celine McQueen - but they should brace themselves for possible heartbreak because he always bails on relationships before things get too serious.

![Image 1: Maxim Baldry as Liam Donovan in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/16/11/1458485431-soaps-hollyoaks-liam-donovan-2922828.jpg?resize=980:*)[![Image 2: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a787507/meet-the-donovans-hollyoaks-introduces-three-new-hunks-as-grace-blacks-brothers-arrive/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/16/11/1458485431-soaps-hollyoaks-liam-donovan-2922828.jpg?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

The cheeky newcomer is delighted by his easy success with the local ladies, but Grace won't be entirely pleased when she realises that her brother has followed her to the village.

Speaking of his role, Baldry told **Digital Spy**: "I'm really excited to be joining the team at _Hollyoaks_. The cast and crew have been super welcoming and helped me settle into life in Liverpool smoothly.

"I can't wait to see what the future holds for Liam, but if his first scenes are anything to go by, he's going to get to know some of the _Hollyoaks_ ladies very well."

Jimmy Essex has been cast as older brother Adam, who'll be making his first appearance on screen in early April. Show insiders have teased that he possesses a strong conscience, which stops him from straying over certain lines that Grace wouldn't think twice about crossing.

![Image 3: Jimmy Essex as Adam Donovan in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/16/11/1458485567-soaps-hollyoaks-jimmy-essex-adam-donovan-29988.jpg?resize=980:*)[![Image 4: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a787507/meet-the-donovans-hollyoaks-introduces-three-new-hunks-as-grace-blacks-brothers-arrive/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/16/11/1458485567-soaps-hollyoaks-jimmy-essex-adam-donovan-29988.jpg?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

Essex told us: "I'm so thrilled to be starting the show. _Hollyoaks_ is already starting to feel like home. Adam has some amazing storylines coming up and I can't wait to share them with the fans. The Donovan brothers are definitely going to cause a stir!"

Finally, Luke Jerdy has landed the role of Jesse, who'll also arrive alongside Adam at the start of next month. He's being billed as a fool for love, who's always unlucky with the ladies because his over-enthusiasm leads to him being friend-zoned.

![Image 5: luke jerdy as jesse donovan in hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/16/11/1458485676-soaps-hollyoaks-luke-jerdy-jesse-donovan-22827.jpg?resize=980:*)[![Image 6: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a787507/meet-the-donovans-hollyoaks-introduces-three-new-hunks-as-grace-blacks-brothers-arrive/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/16/11/1458485676-soaps-hollyoaks-luke-jerdy-jesse-donovan-22827.jpg?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

Jerdy said: "I'm really happy to be joining the team at _Hollyoaks_. There's an exciting collective energy and positive spirit to make the show the best it can be. I'm hoping my character Jesse can bring an infectious enthusiasm and lots of laughter to the screen. He's cheeky, loyal and has a real zest for life."

_Hollyoaks_ previously hinted at the arrival of the new Donovan family [in a sneaky teaser video last month](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a783657/hollyoaks-promises-three-hot-new-hunks-will-arrive-in-this-sneaky-teaser-video/), but the casting and character details had been kept secret until today.

Viewers will get their first glimpse of the brothers in action this afternoon, when _Hollyoaks_ releases an action-packed spring trailer previewing all the drama in store over the next few months.

_Hollyoaks_ will release the promo at 4pm on [its official website](http://www.channel4.com/programmes/hollyoaks) and [YouTube account](https://www.youtube.com/user/hollyoaks).

![Image 7: Liam, Adam and Jesse Donovan in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/16/11/1458485814-soaps-hollyoaks-liam-adam-jesse-donovan-39383883.jpg?resize=980:*)[![Image 8: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a787507/meet-the-donovans-hollyoaks-introduces-three-new-hunks-as-grace-blacks-brothers-arrive/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/16/11/1458485814-soaps-hollyoaks-liam-adam-jesse-donovan-39383883.jpg?resize=1600:*)

An “urban pop” band of best friends who liken themselves to Rihanna are just two shows away from securing a life-changing performance at The O2.

MITSOTU – which stands for Music is the Soul of the Universe – have made it through to the regional finals of the UK’s largest national music competition for original acts, Live and Unsigned.

With around 40,000 musicians entering across the country, the trio of singers will join 60 acts in the Hayes regional live shows battling to make it through to the area finals.

[](https://www.outbrain.com/what-is/default/en)

Holly Cooper, 22, from Petts Wood makes up a third of the band.

She said: “There were about 2,000 people on the day we auditioned just in our region.

“It was amazing because we’ve been doing it in front of our friends and families but this was different and we were quite nervous.

“We’re all best friends and we met at college when we were 16.

“We love to do pop and more commercial things – it’s been great.

“We want to get signed and release amazing music and inspire children.”

This year the annual competition is giving the best acts opportunities to play at some of the country’s biggest festivals including Beach Break Live and Strawberry Fields.

New to 2012, Live and Unsigned is also being filmed for a Sky TV fly-on-the-wall documentary.

![Image 10: News Shopper: Urban pop band MITSOTU reach the brink of success](https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/resources/images/1913879.jpg?type=mds-article-575%20575w)

If MITSOTU triumph in the area finals, they will be performing at London’s biggest indoor festival in July, Live Fest at The O2, before celebrity judges including former Slade front man Noddy Holder and Radio 1’s Annie Nightingale.

Holly added: “This competition is great because it’s for original artists and we sing all our own stuff – it’s not like the X Factor where you have to sing other people’s songs.

“We are like urban pop – like Rihanna but a band.”

James Collins, 22, and Jimmy Essex, also 22, make up the rest of the group.

Since they got together around a year ago, MITSOTU have been travelling around local schools to play for youngsters and inspire them to chase their dreams.

Recently, the trio visited Cooper’s Technology College in Chislehurst and Bishop Justus C of E School in Bromley.

“We perform three songs and give an inspirational speech.” Holly said.

“The response has been amazing – as a kid you want to be star and we tell them you actually can do it if you set your mind to it.

“We tell them they have to work hard to get somewhere and when we leave they are really inspired.

“It’s really rewarding doing what we love and helping others at the same time.”

Acts are competing for the main prizes which include £10,000 to be spent on development, a £10,000 publicity investment, gigs at festivals in Canada, Italy and Latvia, a UK tour of up to 100 shows and a UK festival tour including guaranteed slots at Norfolk Spectacular, Boardmasters, London Summer Jam and Lancaster Music Festival.

* * *

MITSOTU will next perform in their regional finals on Sunday March 11 at the Beck Theatre in Grange Road, Hayes.

12.title: Hollyoaks hints at shock betrayal plot for Adam Donovan
12.description: Hollyoaks is continuing to dole out those mysterious Cards of Fate to its characters ahead of the big Valentine's Day flashforward storyline – and the latest card to be revealed on Instagram is that of Adam Donovan (Jimmy Essex), who's drawn the Backstabber.

Hollyoaks hints at shock betrayal plot for Adam Donovan
=======================================================

He's drawn the Backstabber card in the latest Cards of Fate reveal.

By [Susannah Alexander](https://www.digitalspy.com/author/13517/susannah-alexander/ "Susannah Alexander")Published: 11 February 2018

![Image 9: Jimmy Essex as Adam Donovan in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/06/1518282203-soaps-hollyoaks-jimmy-essex-adam-donovan.jpg?resize=640:*)

Lime Pictures

_Hollyoaks_ is continuing to dole out those mysterious Cards of Fate to its characters ahead of the big Valentine's Day flashforward storyline.

And the latest card to be revealed on Instagram is that of Adam Donovan (Jimmy Essex), who's drawn the Backstabber.

What to Read Next
-----------------

The card, which shows somebody hiding behind a fake face, is captioned: "Is Adam's future plagued with deceit, or can he be saved from his fate? [#CardsOfFate](https://www.instagram.com/explore/tags/cardsoffate/)".

![Image 10: instagram](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/instagram.f282b14.svg?primary=currentColor&id=link-out-embed)[View full post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/BfDSZjChDDF/)

The big question now is, just who is Adam going to betray? There are certainly several characters in the running.

Could it be his sister Grace Black (Tamara Wall)? Or maybe his father Glenn Donovan (Bob Cryer)?

Or is Adam's brother Jesse Donovan (Luke Jerdy) in the firing line? And let's not forget his estranged wife Maxine Blake (Nikki Sanderson).

![Image 11: Adam Donovan lets Maxine Minniver destroy his T-shirts in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/06/1518125182-soaps-hollyoaks-adam-maxine-reunion-hopes-zjvk2ckd46zzmlmlbfy2-3.jpg?resize=980:*)[![Image 12: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a849717/hollyoaks-shock-betrayal-plot-adam-donovan-backstabber-cards-of-fate/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/06/1518125182-soaps-hollyoaks-adam-maxine-reunion-hopes-zjvk2ckd46zzmlmlbfy2-3.jpg?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

The Cards of Fate have already teased [a rocky road ahead for new lovers Myra McQueen and Sally St. Claire](https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/hollyoaks/news/a849669/hollyoaks-rocky-road-for-sally-myra/), as well as [a new development for Marnie Nightingale and one of her children](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a849474/hollyoaks-spoilers-marnie-nightingale-clue/).

It's also been hinted that [there'll be a sad ending for Sami Maalik's revenge mission against James Nightingale](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a849547/hollyoaks-spoilers-sami-james-revenge-outcome/) and that [Cleo McQueen could meet up with evil Pete Buchanan again](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a849432/hollyoaks-spoilers-cleo-mcqueen-devil-teaser/).

Meanwhile, [the Hermit card has been drawn for Peri Lomax](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a849335/hollyoaks-spoilers-peri-lomax-dark-future/), hinting at a dark future now that her lies have been revealed.

![Image 13: Peri Lomax in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/01/1515145745-soaps-hollyoaks-peri-lomax-1.png?resize=980:*)[![Image 14: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a849717/hollyoaks-shock-betrayal-plot-adam-donovan-backstabber-cards-of-fate/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/01/1515145745-soaps-hollyoaks-peri-lomax-1.png?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

We'll see Myra pretending to be a fortune teller at The Dog this week, which will lead to [some special 'time jump' scenes](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a849155/hollyoaks-time-jump-flashforwards-valentinesday-episode-myra-mcqueen/) revealing what's ahead for three families over the next few months.

* * *

**_Hollyoaks_ airs on weeknights at 6.30pm on Channel 4, with first-look screenings at 7pm on E4.**

Harrow band MITSOTU have got through to the area finals of Live & Unsigned, writes Rosy Moorhead
================================================================================================

[Entertainment](https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/topics/entertainment/)

[Music](https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/topics/music/)

By Rosy Moorhead

Share

[](whatsapp://send?text=Three%27s%20a%20crowd%20pleaser%0A%0Ahttps://www.harrowtimes.co.uk%2Fleisure%2Fmusic%2F9645687.harrow-band-mitsotu-have-got-through-to-the-area-finals-of-live-unsigned-writes-rosy-moorhead%2F%3fref%3Dwa)

![Image 2: USA Today logo](https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/resources/responsive-static/images/usa-today-logo.svg)

This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.

Three singers and dancers from Harrow who call themselves MITSOTU are doing rather well in a battle of the bands competition at the moment. But, with a £10,000 prize up for grabs, the prospect of playing festivals across the UK and Europe, a tour and a grand final in London’s The O2, Live & Unsigned is a battle of the bands unlike any other.

Holly Cooper, 22, James Collins, 22, and Jimmy Essex, 23, were one of only five acts to make it through the regional finals at the Beck Theatre in Hayes in March to win a place in the area finals in May.

“We got such a great response,” says James, from north Harrow, “the crowd was amazing. And then one of the judges came up to us afterwards and told us we’d got full marks, he said we were outstanding.”

The three friends seamlessly blended together a song of their own, _Won’t Go Down_, and a cover version of Rihanna’s _You Da One_. After hearing they’d made it through, says James, “we were running about screaming, we had so much adrenaline, we’d put so much into it, that we could have gone on and done a whole show!”

Now the band is busy getting ready for the area finals in May, rehearsing every day, writing new music and doing other gigs. The next round will involve another original and another cover – they will be mixing Labrinth’s _Earthqauke_ with the original _Break Your Heart_.

“We’re really excited,” says James, “we just want to get there and do it. Any chance to get in front of a crowd, we love it.”

James and Jimmy met when they were just seven, at Soul Performing Arts School in Ruislip, and went on to the Urdang Academy of performing arts in Finsbury when they were 16, where they met Holly.

They formed their band, whose name is an acronym of the quote ‘music is the soul of the universe', a year and a half ago and have been performing and producing their blend of pop and rock ever since.

They are playing at _Showcase Live_ at Stamford Bridge on Monday, April 16, an industry night with record label talent scouts and producers in attendance that in the past has played host to Jessie J and JLS, and are planning on releasing their own EP later in the year.

There’s no underestimating just how much a win at Live & Unsigned would mean to MITSOTU. “It would be incredible for us.” James says. “This is the dream.”

MITSOTU are playing in the Live & Unsigned regional finals at The Beck Theatre, Grange Road, Hayes in May. The competition is being screened on Sky TV this summer. Details: www.liveandunsigned.uk.com

Hollyoaks star Jimmy Essex speaks out on Adam's exit in goodbye video
=====================================================================

"I think it's really, really shocking."

By [Rianne Houghton](https://www.digitalspy.com/author/623501/rhoughton/ "Rianne Houghton")Published: 24 May 2018

![Image 7: Adam Donovan in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/21/1526998985-soaps-hollyoaks-adam-donovan-1-tjavlksex2rpvevnkupt-2.png?resize=640:*)

Lime Pictures

After all the recent twists and turns in [_Hollyoaks_](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/), you'd be forgiven for thinking that Adam Donovan might just do a Sienna Blake and return from the dead.

(Wishful thinking, we know.)

What to Read Next
-----------------

Unfortunately for us, that's not the case, as _Hollyoaks_ star Jimmy Essex has officially bid farewell to his character and the soap's cast and crew in his goodbye video.

![Image 8: youtube](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/youtube.ce3e1ae.svg?primary=currentColor&id=link-out-embed)[View full post on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/embed/qBtUj8FnIq8?start=0&enablejsapi=1&origin=https://www.digitalspy.com&autoplay=0)

Reflecting on his two-and-a-half years on the show, Jimmy thanked both the "brilliant"_Hollyoaks_ team and the fans for their support.

Opening up about his exit from 'Oaks, Jimmy admitted that he was "really happy" with Adam's dramatic exit, [where he was shot by his father Glenn](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a857795/hollyoaks-adam-death-fans-react/).

"I think it's really, really shocking. I like the build-up to it – a good guy gone bad and then it turns back round, but then it's too late," he said.

"It makes Bob's character, Glenn, so evil, doesn't it? I like that."

![Image 9: Glenn Donovan is distraught in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/21/1527003140-soaps-hollyoaks-glenn-distraught-16gpxuprk7bievhfpbdnc-1.png?resize=980:*)[![Image 10: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a857903/hollyoaks-cast-jimmy-essex-adam-donovan-exit/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/21/1527003140-soaps-hollyoaks-glenn-distraught-16gpxuprk7bievhfpbdnc-1.png?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

**Related:**[**Hollyoaks reveals Glenn Donovan fightback as Maxine agrees to help the police**](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a857828/hollyoaks-spoilers-glenn-donovan-maxine-fightback/)

Bob Cryer, who plays the sinister Glenn, is also quite fond of the Donovans' storyline, telling **Digital Spy** that it's ["great fun to play" such a baddie](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/interviews/a857475/hollyoaks-bob-cryer-depression-glenn-donovan-future/).

Hinting that fans may have to wait a while for Glenn's comeuppance, Bob said of his character's future: "I just take each day as it comes.

"But Glenn is definitely running out of friends – if he had any to begin with!"
