This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.

AN X FACTOR contestant, from Petts Wood, believes that her “urban pop” band can go all the way in the talent competition.

Holly Cooper, 23, of Woodhurst Avenue, is a part of MITSOTU - which stands for Music Is The Soul Of The Universe - who will find out if they have made the live shows this Saturday (29).

If the trio including James Collins, 22, and Jimmy Essex, 23, both from Harrow, make the final stage of the competition, Miss Cooper says, it will come as no surprise to them.

The part-time hospital worker said: “We do think that we could go all the way because there has never been anyone like us before.

“We are not really like any other band but we love Rihanna and No Doubt.”

MISTOTU did their first audition back in June in front of a 6,000 strong audience.

However, despite the daunting crowd they put on a brilliant performance to score four “yes” votes securing their path to the next stage.

Miss Cooper says the toughest stage but, also, the most enjoyable was the boot camp in Liverpool.

She said: “More than 200 performers were sent home after only couple of hours without even singing.

“It was harsh but that is reality TV.

“Boot camp was the hardest thing we have ever done.”

The reason for MISTOTU’s progress through the competition, according to Miss Cooper, is the experience they have had of performing live.

All three members have all performed with world famous pop stars as backing dancers: Miss Cooper with The Wanted, Mr Collins has danced with The Saturdays and Mr Essex has performed alongside Janet Jackson.

However, despite their experience the group had their doubts about Louis Walsh, who is mentoring the group.

Miss Copper added: “At first because we are an urban pop group we thought 'oh, we got Louis' but he is really cool.”

The group, who each have the tattoo MITSOTU on their left arm, toured schools across the borough last year to play for youngsters.

But if they are put through on Saturday night’s X Factor show then the band can maybe dream of playing across the world once again as MITSOTU.

14.title: Inside Soap Awards 2018 full longlist revealed: Which Corrie, EastEnders, Emmerdale and Hollyoaks stars are up?
14.description: The Inside Soap Awards 2018 are back, and it's time to start voting for your favourite soap stars once again. Which Coronation Street, EastEnders, Emmerdale and Hollyoaks stars are nominated?
14.content:
It's that time of the year again – time to start voting for all of your favourite soaps at the Inside Soap Awards.

It's already shaping up to be a great year with plenty of competition, as _[Coronation Street](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/news/a862219/coronation-street-shayne-ward-inside-soap-awards/)_'s [Shayne Ward is among the nominees for Best Actor](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/news/a862219/coronation-street-shayne-ward-inside-soap-awards/), where he'll be up against _[EastEnders](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/eastenders)_' Danny Dyer, _[Emmerdale](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/emmerdale/news/a862238/emmerdale-ash-palmisciano-inside-soap-awards/)_'s Ryan Hawley and _[Hollyoaks](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/)_' Gregory Finnegan – to name just a few of the other contenders.

_Emmerdale_[newcomer Ash Palmisciano](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/emmerdale/news/a858892/emmerdale-spoilers-matty-barton-ash-palmisciano/) (Matty Barton) has also [landed his first ever soap award nomination](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/emmerdale/news/a862238/emmerdale-ash-palmisciano-inside-soap-awards/) in the awards, picking up a nod for Best Newcomer, where he'll be up against the likes of _Corrie_'s Alexandra Mardell (Emma Brooker) and _EastEnders_' Katie Jarvis (Hayley Slater) for the award.

![Image 1: Katie Jarvis as Hayley Slater in EastEnders](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/09/1519753900-15173577-high-res-eastenders-portraits-2018.jpg?resize=980:*)[![Image 2: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a862268/inside-soap-awards-2018-full-longlist-coronation-street-eastenders-emmerdale-hollyoaks/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/09/1519753900-15173577-high-res-eastenders-portraits-2018.jpg?resize=1600:*)

BBC

Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

But those are just two of the 18 categories that readers can vote for, and the official longlist of nominations reveals a few tough categories too.

Fighting for the title of Best Bad Boy will see _Coronation Street_'s Connor McIntyre (Pat Phelan) and Ryan Clayton (Josh Tucker) go against _EastEnders_' Ricky Champ (Stuart Highway) and Charlie Winter (Hunter Owen), while Thomas Atkinson (Lachlan White) and Ned Porteous (Joe Tate) represent _Emmerdale_'s chances, and Bob Cryer (Glenn Donovan) and Duncan James (Ryan Knight) fight for _Hollyoaks_.

Meanwhile, _EastEnders_' heartbreaking [Shakil and Keegan knife attack storyline](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/eastenders/feature/a858049/eastenders-shakil-knife-crime-story-review/) is in the running for Best Show-Stopper, alongside the likes of Aidan taking his own life in _Corrie_ and [the Whites' car crash](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/emmerdale/feature/a847170/emmerdale-spoilers-white-family-crash-who-dies/) in _Emmerdale_.

![Image 3: Chrissie White in the Emmerdale crash](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/02/1515698175-soaps-emmerdale-chrissie-white-crash-gqg6arjf8nwiu5g4litp.jpg?resize=980:*)[![Image 4: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a862268/inside-soap-awards-2018-full-longlist-coronation-street-eastenders-emmerdale-hollyoaks/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/02/1515698175-soaps-emmerdale-chrissie-white-crash-gqg6arjf8nwiu5g4litp.jpg?resize=1600:*)

### Happy Ending ★★★★ Waterloo East Theatre | Sep 27 - Oct 26, 2025

[![Image 1: Two men in casual wear are on the stage, near the massage table, in front of blinds, during a performance](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEguemvFMAJdq7gfoCC2xpd9diq4opyGQ3AAFkjB5ZPtqWaxumjX0tNNKe-dFIfXTfkm1aOqRn3DJQpuJ5AFoz0-PKAa3QAYV-iLtasDeoJu-FSdew_RxulE6AtC_12qddj8oouIZOhGRG8e3gpSSbEP7jDjxHb3h37DwgT5oIoSJuRQ-BQihM5fM7F52aI/w640-h513/Billy_Walker_and_Jimmy_Essex_3_credit_Gareth_McLeod.jpg)](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEguemvFMAJdq7gfoCC2xpd9diq4opyGQ3AAFkjB5ZPtqWaxumjX0tNNKe-dFIfXTfkm1aOqRn3DJQpuJ5AFoz0-PKAa3QAYV-iLtasDeoJu-FSdew_RxulE6AtC_12qddj8oouIZOhGRG8e3gpSSbEP7jDjxHb3h37DwgT5oIoSJuRQ-BQihM5fM7F52aI/s5296/Billy_Walker_and_Jimmy_Essex_3_credit_Gareth_McLeod.jpg)

Ronnie Larsen has written an amusing two-hander that, along with some witty dialogue, reveals uncomfortable truths about the complex roles that prevarication and fantasy play in people’s lives. Jimmy Essex portrays Andy, a gay masseur who must navigate the advances of a straight client, Mr. Millar, played by Billy Walker. Andy doesn’t want to cross professional lines and risk his license, yet Mr. Millar possesses many of the qualities that he finds attractive. What follows is a cat-and-mouse seduction that ultimately exposes hidden aspects of both men. Larsen delivers a sharp, intimate piece that uses the physical closeness of massage as a metaphor for what becomes a deeper, soul-baring exchange. Both Essex and Walker strike the right balance of awkwardness and manipulation as they circle each other, and their discomfort and attraction are equally palpable. The play subtly offers some insight not only into the small deceptions we all employ to get through life but into the restricting nature of our fantasies. _Happy Ending_ proves to be a thoughtful, well-acted work that delivers exactly what its title promises – and perhaps a little extra.

Rated: ★★★★

Reviewed by J.C.

Photo by Gareth McLeod

### [The Playboy of the Western World ★★★★ National Theatre | Until February 28, 2026](http://www.londonlivinglarge.com/2025/12/the-playboy-of-western-world-national.html)

[![Image 2: A man in period costume sits at a table looking up at a blonde woman in a green dress who is leaning over him](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjBN2-L-lHsNre_S4FOG2dwKeT2WG4bHHXsZB3aMCcPfr2vPeW9stxDi1FQ2pxlRSrH8433znAITCA1hCJoo1AU2DN4bo4h2D5gF2ww4ZM5fzQ9AnW80c_kpqzJHOpefF7uwwm4MCWt2g2_9QGDcHGCmnrkv-Kl2RJx_27TPA-x7pj8KLqH3CisqhpQ_ic/w640-h427/E%CC%81anna%20Hardwicke%20(Christy%20Mahon)%20and%20Nicola%20Coughlan%20(Pegeen%20Mike)%20in%20The%20Playboy%20of%20the%20Western%20World%20at%20the%20National%20Theatre.%20(c)%20Marc%20Brenner%200003.jpg)](http://www.londonlivinglarge.com/2025/12/the-playboy-of-western-world-national.html)

John Millington Synge’s The Playboy of the Western World is a work rich in significance and open to varied interpretation. In his programme notes, Christopher Collins views the play through the contemporary lens of the global migrant crisis and society’s fascination with celebrity. Yet Christy Mahon’s (Christ as Man) symbolic killing of his father, who returns with amusing regularity, also invites a reading of the play as a religious satire in which Synge advances a vision of bold and irreverent humanism. In many respects, this is a radically innovative piece of writing that challenges both social expectations and the established conventions of comedy. This current National Theatre production preserves much of the original’s force and the stark and lyrical set vividly conjures the atmosphere of the west of Ireland. As the eponymous hero, Éanna Hardwicke convincingly portrays the timid youth who, through the fantasies of the townspeople, discovers his identity and is reborn as a figure...

### [Beauty and the Beast: A Horny Love Story ★★★★★ Charing Cross Theatre | Nov 21, 2025 - Jan 11, 2026](http://www.londonlivinglarge.com/2025/12/beauty-and-beast-horny-love-story.html)

[![Image 3: Man dressed in drag, with bright orange curly hair and a tartan hat, stands with arms outstretched against a stage backdrop resembling an old-fashioned garage with shelves of motor products](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEh1icgp5Fpwti4PGuKtuSBhaabkk_JsFoiiES_Czj9YGHZqxq_ZkY3UmrYDplJ79fEvEzN4ai8KlioiXGurw3gJT5V1h9lBqVzMQpi5-DmwkTPrZAbnWX_-eq1StdhRIoMxXlauTncBfP161D56gai62d-pD-wPDourrxt4vGOsxxqOlen8FczvgAJUXAs/w640-h426/BATBAHLS%20-%20Matthew%20Baldwin%20-%20Credit%20SteveGregson-034.jpg)](http://www.londonlivinglarge.com/2025/12/beauty-and-beast-horny-love-story.html)

This year’s big and gloriously gay panto from the “He’s Behind You!” gang has burst into the Charing Cross Theatre, and it has arrived like it owns the place. Beauty and the Beast: A Horny Love Story brings back several familiar faces, including the incomparable Matthew Baldwin, who now plays the mother of two gay children living at a petrol station in the Scottish Highlands. Baldwin is every bit as majestic as you imagine a woman in a fluorescent tabard can be. Laura Anna-Mead playing Bonnie, the frequently ignored lesbian daughter, bounces through the show with a delightful energy, while Matt Kennedy completely charms as Bertie, the titular beauty. As his beastly counterpart Keanu Adolphus Johnson is ferociously fabulous. Chris Lane earns his boos and hisses as Cornelius, the villainous brother whose moral compass has a limp arrow, while Dani Mirels deserves her cheers as the blue-haired enchantress who finds love. However, again this year, it is Baldwin who storms the stage. With a...

### [My Fair Lady ★★★★★ The Mill at Sonning | Nov 20, 2025 - Jan 17, 2026](http://www.londonlivinglarge.com/2025/11/my-fair-lady-mill-at-sonning-nov-20.html)

[![Image 4: The group of actors is on the stage performing on a musical stage with metal garbage cans and kitchen utensils](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhcoOfGYD0dbXszhOv3hgl5uabcRh-Rc9VPu8GzvsQ5mIOCnQk8lZtQp-w9x_04SsIaoa9lzz_xIJ91cBcLMpUiVRQVHokk3mU6ysZ6n3s9Fcqqq1PvQuXAG2BDpsQhuYK7l3JcU5Vzd1RXnFPYXLewj-cGmiwqtzbgtdSs3PRjzsytroW-vANxW_ZGcYM/w640-h380/My%20Fair%20Lady%20Mill%20at%20Sonning%20Mark%20Moraghan%20and%20the%20cast%20Pamela%20Raith%20Photography.jpg)](http://www.londonlivinglarge.com/2025/11/my-fair-lady-mill-at-sonning-nov-20.html)

It is easy to misremember Lerner and Loewe’s My Fair Lady as simply another musical romcom, but this superb production reminds us that it is rooted in George Bernard Shaw’s Pygmalion . Along with the beguiling love story, there is a sharp and insightful commentary on class, gender, and the social forces that shape us. This is a transformation tale with something to say, and this first-rate staging gets the balance exactly right between fairy tale romance and pointed social critique. The beloved story of the Cockney flower girl who blossoms into a lady and the brilliant but blinkered academic, who finds he has a heart after all, is presented with uncommon clarity and warmth. It is not only the tale of Eliza’s metamorphosis, a working class woman discovering her independence, her identity, and her voice. It is also about the detached and self assured middle class academic Henry Higgins learning, sometimes painfully, what it means to truly listen. Simbi Akande is a radiant Eliza Doolittl...

### [David Copperfield ★★★★ Jermyn Street Theatre | Nov 20 - Dec 20, 2025](http://www.londonlivinglarge.com/2025/11/david-copperfield-jermyn-street-theatre.html)

[![Image 5: Performer on stage raises a top hat in one hand, while holding a large scroll in the other hand](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgOqrt3vRQTlE5R7V60EZXty_G9kBtWZEx8MS0OUqISzENJkeM-viqZsLzWDASWYxfmouQqyCX57ynvPsYw5TkO9njIzsu2i0l35O1KaB7tdWBz-zcKnDhctD-uuTf8lQEn2awLSstFv0kX1RiXB8rDuHk7Oz1K0PA2BEUNOe9lE2f-wIUKixbuiaHo5Y0/w640-h426/Eddy%20Payne%20-%20credit%20Steve%20Gregson.jpg)](http://www.londonlivinglarge.com/2025/11/david-copperfield-jermyn-street-theatre.html)

It seems like an impossible task. Can you really squeeze all of the incidents and characters of one of Dickens' sprawling novels into a two-hour theatrical production and have all of the people played by only three actors? Amazingly, the Guildford Shakespeare Company manages to do just that. This theatrical version of Dickens' semi-autobiographical masterpiece is remarkably faithful to the original story, and somehow the small cast brings to life each of the author's wonderfully eccentric creations. From the ever optimistic Mr Micawber to the unctuous Uriah Heep every figure David Copperfield encounters on his life-journey becomes a believable and engaging personage. As in the novel, we begin at the moment of David's birth and end with his marriage to a paragon of Victorian virtue. Along the way we are introduced to a plethora of weird characters and must navigate a convoluted plot that is riddled with coincidence. Refreshingly in this telling, the familiar Dickensian...

### [All My Sons ★★★★★ Wyndham’s Theatre | Until March 7, 2026](http://www.londonlivinglarge.com/2025/11/all-my-sons-wyndhams-theatre-until.html)

[![Image 6: Four persons sitting on a mud-coated trunk of tree, with the set a mud-coated wall, a black square shape on the wall](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhcHDRhfM1G502bhgN9A0JhH7xLHLDXZgQSid4jBmr1w4guUM2eUH1vCEwT1aw70p7YpBZgUteIPDPxG7DE_SWOiy5DQFu0hna7X6maTBf5s4JYDLf3rE-lwbUhVaHONOAAVG6R6U-2FWu-OloRCACNyPRia2ZKxAFROiZzrzPvaEokC6j4Q6xb4MkQAnA/w640-h427/ALL%20MY%20SONS.%20Bryan%20Cranston%20(Joe%20Keller),%20Marianne%20Jean-Baptiste%20(Kate%20Keller),%20Hayley%20Squires%20(Ann%20Deever)%20and%20Paapa%20Essiedu%20(Chris%20Keller).%20Photo%20Jan%20Versweyveld.jpg)](http://www.londonlivinglarge.com/2025/11/all-my-sons-wyndhams-theatre-until.html)

Bryan Cranston’s star shines brightly in Ivo Van Hove’s splendid revival of Arthur Miller’s 1946 masterpiece. Cranston is a completely compelling presence as Joe Keller, the kindly older businessman who plays imaginary games with neighbourhood children. His portrayal is simply remarkable as this pleasant veneer is peeled away and the war profiteer and self-serving sophist beneath it are revealed. The games he shares with the children echo the ones he plays with his family and friends, whom he draws into colluding with his pretence of innocence and with the web of rationalisations he has spun for his past actions. Miller’s work carries an epic weight that Van Hove captures with his sparse staging, and Cranston’s performance evokes the moral authority and emotional force of Greek tragedy. As Joe’s wife, Kate, whose belief in her husband is tied to her certainty that her son survived the war, Marianne Jean-Baptiste also gives an unforgettable performance. The strong cast is completed by P...

End is the third play in David Eldridge's trilogy about couples at different stages of their relationships. In this final instalment, Alfie (Clive Owens) and Julie (Saskia Reeves) confront Alfie’s imminent death from cancer. Their exchanges are at once humorous and deeply affecting as they revisit memories, moments of happiness, regrets, and past conflicts. Plans for the funeral become conversations about dying and tentative imaginings of what might lie ahead. Each of the three plays is set in the morning, a liminal period between night and day that suggests transition and vulnerability. However, in this instance, the strictly limited timeframe feels somewhat contrived. Too much is compressed into a span that in reality would unfold over several days. Dividing the play into a series of distinct scenes with overlapping discussions might have made for greater verisimilitude and prevented some of the abrupt changes in tone and subject matter. Ready at last to abandon the service, he is instead drawn into a final, intricate scheme meant to topple his old adversary, Mundt, head of East Germany’s foreign intelligence apparatus. The alcohol and the banter are flowing, and we seem to be in familiar comedic territory until an argument breaks out over gay marriage. Mitchell, a writer and Daniel’s partner, considers marriage an unnecessary, heteronormative expression of commitment. The remainder of the play is about Mitchell, and the audience, learning the importance of the institution of marriage for gay couples. Despite some clever dialogue and some good character development, this work is mainly didactic, and when Daniel falls ill, there is an uneasy sense of emotional manipulation which accompanies the lesson that we are being taught. The play also glosses over the truly formidable realities faced by caregivers when a partner develops a chronic condition. [![Image 11: Two women are on a stage with greenery, a dark background, and white confetti falling from above](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjOXzhepwogS1-6wOY3DHc7-kaDcvesvKwDavVbDGOs_YQ4DNgK2uCxhhXhflEtZHvT8U822s7Dg6CaQ-XN3YiSp6TtZSPP-M79fEbVFGRj-WV8LZWuRBI-BluKIpg7njX6B_aqgbhRFWFxODntZfjn1FYu34uG3XYakz5gAA2gmo1-x6VmR8n2qUy5HCo/w640-h427/Felicity%20Kendal%20(Mrs%20Swan)%20and%20Ruby%20Ashbourne%20Serkis%20(Flora%20Crewe)%20in%20Indian%20Ink%E2%80%9305243_credit%20Johan%20Persson.jpg)](http://www.londonlivinglarge.com/2025/12/indian-ink-hampstead-theatre-dec-3-jan.html)

This first-rate production of Tom Stoppard’s palimpsestic masterpiece is simply a must-see. When the English poet Flora Crewe travels to India, she sits for a portrait by the Indian painter Nirad Das. Both that portrait and this play reflect the complex melding of cultures that emerged from the British presence in India. Exploring different approaches to art and the presentation of the artist, the drama also exposes the intricate and often fraught political relationship between the two countries whose histories became so deeply intertwined. Flora’s meeting with the Indian painter hints at the complicated dynamic between a dying imperial vision and its colonial subject, while also questioning the epistemological frameworks through which we seek to understand the past. Many years later, Crewe's American biographer meets with her sister Mrs Swan as he attempts to reconstruct that Indian encounter. Three new faces are set to join the cast of Hollyoaks as The Donovans arrive in town – three cheeky brothers who will make a big impression.

Jimmy Essex, Maxim Baldry and Luke Jerdy will make their debut in the Channel 4 soap, playing “bold and brazen” trio Adam, Liam and Jesse Donovan.

![Image 4: The Donovans ](http://snappa.static.pressassociation.io/assets/2016/03/21140257/1458568974-cb34ad54ed9f6d71fc4ccdaf6bcbf068-600x400.jpg)

The Donovans (Lime Pictures)

The Donovans are half-brothers to Grace Black (Tamara Wall), and will pop up in April to bicker over girls and fight over hair gel. But above all, they will remain bound by brotherly affection.

So who are they?

Adam Donovan
------------

![Image 5: Adam Donovan](http://snappa.static.pressassociation.io/assets/2016/03/21134334/1458567810-a4edbdf241bacd1f1f9f92cb659c12d1-600x901.jpg)

Adam Donovan (Lime Pictures)

The eldest of the family, Adam bears very little resemblance to his half-sister in terms of personality. He has a strong conscience – and won’t stray over the line.

Jimmy said: “I’m so thrilled to be starting the show, Hollyoaks is already starting to feel like home.

“Adam has some amazing storylines coming up and I can’t wait to share them with the fans. The Donovan brothers are definitely going to cause a stir!”

Liam Donovan
------------

![Image 6: Liam Donovan](http://snappa.static.pressassociation.io/assets/2016/03/21134445/1458567882-460e856cfb1904db495f5d328dbf78b7-600x900.jpg)

Liam Donovan (Lime Pictures)

Liam is more brooding than his older brother. A hit with women, he’s not too good at commitment and “always bails before they get too attached”.

Maxim said: “I can’t wait to see what the future holds for Liam but if his first scenes are anything to go by, he’s going to get to know some of the Hollyoaks ladies very well…”

Jesse Donovan
-------------

![Image 7: Jesse Donovan ](http://snappa.static.pressassociation.io/assets/2016/03/21134547/1458567943-cf244a6b7cbc6bb8bdd2dbd79892344f-600x901.jpg)

Jesse Donovan (Lime Pictures)

Over-enthusiastic youngest brother Jesse is a “fool for love” but not always so lucky in his romantic life.

Luke said: “I’m hoping my character Jesse can bring an infectious enthusiasm and lots of laughter to the screen. He’s cheeky, loyal and has a real zest for life.”

![Image 8: The Donovans at The Loft ](http://snappa.static.pressassociation.io/assets/2016/03/21135932/1458568769-9a75bfa5904b2de080917ffe24fddb98-600x400.jpg)

The Donovans at The Loft (Lime Pictures)

Review: HAPPY ENDING at Waterloo East Theatre
=============================================

![Image 2: Stuart King](https://www.londonboxoffice.co.uk/news/public/authors/.sking_t.jpg)[Stuart King](https://www.londonboxoffice.co.uk/news/author/sking) 1 October, 2025, 09:55

Back in 2009 Gerald Armin stumbled upon an abandoned railway arch in Waterloo East and decided — wait for it — that despite inherent challenges, with a little love and attention, it would make a great off-West End theatre! It goes to prove that sometimes the daftest ideas will gain traction. Opening the following year, the intimate venue has since hosted over 300 productions and continues to present plays with a distinctly gay flavour for its appreciative audiences.

![Image 3: happy ending waterloo east](https://www.londonboxoffice.co.uk/news/public/happy_ending_waterloo_east_review.jpg)

_Andrew_ (**Jimmy Essex**) having put himself through college and qualified in massage therapy, now runs a small Florida practise and is building a solid base of satisfied clients. _Mr Millar_ (**Billy Walker**) is a plaid wearing, self-confessed blue collar Trump supporter and works opposite at a carpet warehouse where he has developed back and shoulder problems. What at first seems like a fairly hum-drum client session, turns into a grilling about sexuality, bumper stickers on Volvo’s, political affiliations, nudity, the appeals of _heteroflexibility_, what’s included in the session price, and what practises are most definitely against the rules during such an transactional encounter.

On its own, the scenario would make for a blandly predictable, even irritating play, but during the course of their initially fractious discourse about Adele vs Steely Dan (at no point are Andean pan-pipes nor whale music ever considered as options to accompany the massage), the men circle each other, with Millar (“…call me Rick, no one calls me Mr Millar”) becoming evermore appreciative of the rub-down and inquisitive about how often Andrew gets asked to perform ‘extras’.

Of course there has to be something more going on than the simple set-up we are initially presented with, and sure enough, revelations and a few admissions quickly bubble to the surface as accusations fly, morals slip and a truly happy ending is reached. Whilst some, dimly-lit sexual activity is implied during the course of proceedings, the play is at great pains to suggest that two needy souls may in fact have the basis for a more interesting and substantial connection — although arriving at that conclusion is something of a narrative stretch given the lies and creepy stalking which has evidently taken place to ensure the characters end up in the same room, but sometimes you just have to surrender to the flow and park one’s in-built 21st century cynicism.

Writer/Director **Ronnie Larson** has wisely corralled his players into a limiting playing area on a perfunctory set which is sufficiently redolent of a massage therapy room with its central table, privacy screens, potted plants and dazzling array of oils and potions, to pass muster. In truth, given the play’s title, I was cautious about accepting the invitation to review, but thankfully the performers imbue a winning charm (and plenty of gleaming LA teeth) to their efforts, which goes a long way to helping matters when an audience is eagerly rooting for those about _to root_ on stage.

**_HAPPY ENDING_** continues at Waterloo East until 26th October.

We chatted to Jimmy about entering the theatre industry in a pandemic, the misconceptions of gay culture that the show addresses and why he loves playing challenging roles.

**Can you explain the story of _GHBoy_, and the role of Robert, who you're playing?**

The story is centred around Robert and his addiction to chemsex and cheating. It's about his discovery of himself, finding out who he is and coming to terms with something really terrible that happened to him and the major effect it's had on his life.

**How are you feeling about making your West End debut?**

Amazing, and it's been the most incredible experience so far. Coming into something so new and exciting in itself feels like such an achievement.

It's something very different to anything I've ever done and I just love the challenge of it. I couldn't be happier really.

**Does it feel odd to be making your debut during a pandemic?**

Yeah, of course. But the good thing is, I have nothing to compare it to!

I didn't know how it was going to work; to an extent, you're making the rules as you go along because nobody's faced this before, so we're just figuring things out as we go.

There have been a few growing pains, but I think we're there now. We get how it has to work and how we can do it safely; it's been challenging, but also really exciting.

**What drew you to go from your TV work to the theatre?**

I love theatre, and theatre is what got me into acting anyway. I think as a medium, it's incredible; there's something so magical about it.

I also wanted to push myself, and I love this role of Robert. I think the role really spoke to me; there's something about his journey of discovering himself that really scratched an itch for me, so I just jumped at the chance.

![Image 40: Interview: Jimmy Essex Talks GHBOY at Charing Cross Theatre  Image](https://cloudimages2.broadwayworld.com/upload13/2076432/Jimmy-Essex-Robert-Finch-Marc-Bosch-Sergi-Castell_-Credit-Adam-Stevens-Productions-768x432.jpg?format=auto&width=1400)

Jimmy Essex & Marc Bosch

 in _GHBoy_

**How are rehearsals going?**

Great! They've been going really well.

We're obviously having to do social distancing, we're getting tested quite regularly and we have to wear masks for some of it too. So it's all been learning how to adapt to this crazy new world we're living in.

But it's been great - the cast is wonderful and the director, Jon Pashley is amazing. I know Paul Harvard, who wrote the play, from years and years ago, so it's been nice to reconnect with him as well.

**It's Paul Harvard's debut play - is it nice to star in someone's debut work as your West End debut?**

Yeah, definitely. I think because it's new and it's his first play, everyone wants to make it as amazing as it can be, just out of the love for it and because we want to make it special for everyone.

Plus, we're the first people doing it, so there's something really exciting about that. We're paving the way for it, which is lovely.

**The show tackles misconceptions around gay culture and promiscuity - why is this such an important message?**

I think there are taboos and a hushness around a lot of gay culture; not just from the heterosexual community to the gay community, but also within the gay community too. There are a lot of misconceptions and stigma that come with certain lifestyles and choices. So, I think it's really good to put a human face on this subject and make it relatable. I just think it's really important to shine a light on it.

**The show has a very diverse cast with a range of ages and experiences, both on stage and behind the scenes. That must be a great team to be part of.**

Yeah, definitely. I think we all feel very blessed. Not only because we're trying to do something that seems impossible, but also because of the range of people involved and the experiences they're bringing to the project.

I think it says so much about what we want the message to be; it's about acceptance of everyone.

![Image 41: Interview: Jimmy Essex Talks GHBOY at Charing Cross Theatre  Image](https://cloudimages2.broadwayworld.com/upload13/2076432/Sylvester-Akinrolabu-Jimmy-Essex-Robert-Finch_-Credit-Adam-Stevens-Productions.jpg?format=auto&width=1400)

Jimmy Essex and Sylvester Akinrolabu

 in _GHBoy_

**It's been a really weird year. How have you been coping during the pandemic?**

To be honest, at first, I loved it. Once I focused on just getting back to basics, appreciating what I have and the people I have around me, as well as the magic and the enjoyment in everyday life, there was something really special about that. I loved it.

Then about halfway through, I was pulling my hair out. I'm quite an active person and I love to be doing things, and so it's been quite a struggle.

I think the one good thing I took from it was the fact I was with my partner the whole time and we got to actually spend some time together, which is a rarity. And also, just finding enjoyment; my garden has never looked so good!

**You're about to make your debut, but what would your dream theatre role be in the future?**

Any kind of theatre that inspires some kind of conversation, and a role that is as challenging as Robert in _GHBoy_.

I think those are the things that I look forward to, and as I'm growing in my career, are things that make me question myself and normatives that I may have already created in my own brain.

Those juicy roles where it changes not only the audience, but my perspective of things, that's what appeals to me the most.

**Why should people come and see _GHBoy_?**

We're putting on this amazing show, so come and support theatre!

I think it will surprise people too. I think people have a misconception about what the play is going to be about and how they're going to feel about it. I think they'll walk out with a completely new mindset, having gone on this amazing journey with this guy. I think there's something really, really special about that.

_GHBoy at Charing Cross Theatre [from 3 December](http://Tickets are available now)_

21.title: Review: Happy Ending (Waterloo East Theatre)
21.content:
**Review by Oliver Briggs**

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

There are few plays as surprising, intimate and disarming yet comedic as _Happy Ending_, now playing at Waterloo East Theatre. A thoroughly modern play with the first notable production in 2017 in Florida, as well as performances in London in 2018, and at the Garden Theatre summer Festival in 2021. I had high expectations having familiarised myself with the show's history, and not only were these expectations met, they were actually exceeded.

![Image 1: ree](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/d63317_844af4e4b64847e289310443ee51110c~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_740,h_516,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/d63317_844af4e4b64847e289310443ee51110c~mv2.jpg)

Written and directed by Ronnie Larsen, _Happy Ending_ is an 80 minute comedy centered around a single massage session between Andrew, a meticulous and openly gay massage therapist, and his new client, Mr Miller, a brash, conservative-leaning man who proudly identifies as a MAGA-supporting, Trump-voting straight guy. At first glance, their interaction appears rife with tension, as their contrasting personalities clash; Andrew's tidy professionalism versus Mr Miller's rough and careless demeanor. Their exchanges are laced with comedic misunderstandings and subtle jabs, particularly around Mr Miller’s paranoia about Andrew’s sexuality affecting the session and his casual disregard for Andrew’s space, but was this who Mr Miller really played himself to be? There is still far more of the story.

Almost entirely designed by the Waterloo East Theatre, the set is beautiful - pristine, clean and well-kept, made to resemble the studio of a massage therapist, with thin paper curtains that let gentle, warm light through, and exposed wooden beams at the back creating a warm and welcome environment. The walls were angled which was particularly effective focusing the audience's sight. To important actions. Props like plants, oils, water bottles filled the space and reinforced the believability that I was in a massage therapy studio.

![Image 2: ree](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/d63317_1657e4c2ae574b7dba04083bd5bf3052~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_740,h_631,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/d63317_1657e4c2ae574b7dba04083bd5bf3052~mv2.jpg)

Equally strong is Jonathan Simpson's lighting design, creating a bright and calm space with warmer tones in areas creating an intimate and heated environment that beautifully complemented the set design.

The individual character performances in _Happy Ending_ were astonishing. Jimmy Essex brought to his character, Andrew, a subtle yet very present flamboyance to the stage, through all of his smaller movements, the way he held his arms, each and every little facial gesture, lip lick, jaw-dropped moment was met with fluttered demeanour. His attraction to Mr Miller seeps through the way his eyes lock with Mr Miller's entire body.

![Image 3: ree](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/d63317_c9d2d9124936444d851dba125c9ae32c~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_147,h_118,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/d63317_c9d2d9124936444d851dba125c9ae32c~mv2.jpg)

Billy Walker carried a massively masculine gait about him originally, very tall, very stiff. A slightly deeper voice with more tension throughout his body, and he has a great character development as his performance becomes somewhat looser and free over time with how his characters' secrets are revealed. Both performers displayed intense chemistry and heated intimacy, with immense and subtle facial expressions.

Overall the production excels with its remarkable set and costume design, alongside the crazy chemistry of the actors and their detailed and nuanced choices under Larsen’s witty writing and direction. With stellar comedic performances, a sensitively designed set, and unexpected emotional weight, _Happy Ending_ guarantees to give you what the title suggests.

![Image 4: ree](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/d63317_b5fa7a095ed44e92bbca60aeb62657f0~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_147,h_85,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/d63317_b5fa7a095ed44e92bbca60aeb62657f0~mv2.jpg)

Odd disturbances shake up [The Dreaming](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/The_Dreaming "The Dreaming"), [Rose](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Rose_Walker_(Netflix) "Rose Walker (Netflix)") sets out on a road trip with a [new friend](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Gilbert_(Netflix) "Gilbert (Netflix)"), and [The Corinthian](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/The_Corinthian_(Netflix) "The Corinthian (Netflix)") arrives with a [guest](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Jed_Walker_(Netflix) "Jed Walker (Netflix)") at a creepy convention.

Plot[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsandman.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FChapter_9%3A_Collectors%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D2&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[![Image 3: Lyta's baby bump](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sandman/images/0/0e/Netflix_The_Sandman_109_Collectors_03_Lyta.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/250?cb=20220810163739)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sandman/images/0/0e/Netflix_The_Sandman_109_Collectors_03_Lyta.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20220810163739)

Lyta's baby bump

[Rose](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Rose_Walker_(Netflix) "Rose Walker (Netflix)") informed [Lyta](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Lyta_Hall_(Netflix) "Lyta Hall (Netflix)") of her dreams and how she dreamt of finding [Jed](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Jed_Walker_(Netflix) "Jed Walker (Netflix)"), who told her where his foster parents lived. So she went there, but when she arrived, Jed was gone and they were dead. As strange as it sounded, Lyta believed Rose because she also had a dream where she was with [Hector](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Hector_Hall_(Netflix) "Hector Hall (Netflix)"). And when she woke up, she was still pregnant, unsure of how this could've happened. And so, Rose explained to Lyta how she was a [vortex](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Dream_Vortex "Dream Vortex") and likely the cause of this.

[Matthew](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Matthew_(Netflix) "Matthew (Netflix)") reported back to [Lucienne](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Lucienne_(Netflix) "Lucienne (Netflix)") that Lyta was pregnant from a dream, meaning Rose was weakening the walls between realms. However, Lucienne had no intentions of relaying the message to [Dream](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Dream_(Netflix) "Dream (Netflix)") herself, as he reminded her that she was merely a librarian. He was determined to deal with the vortex alone, so Lucienne instructed Matthew to report any updates exclusively to Dream.

[The Corinthian](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/The_Corinthian_(Netflix) "The Corinthian (Netflix)") and Jed stopped for ice cream and discussed their plans to meet Rose at a convention he'd be attending. Jed then asked The Corinthian his name. Rather than answer, he replied by telling Jed that people only ever used someone's name when they were in trouble, similar to how [Barnaby](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Barnaby_Farrell "Barnaby Farrell") would call out to Jed. However, Corinthian assured him that Barnaby would no longer be a problem. He also shared with Jed how much like him he was, also running away from something, but once they got to Rose, they'd never need to run again.

Rose wasn't sure how or when she was even doing it, but she assured Lyta she'd fix her mistake and make it go away. Lyta saw this as a second chance at life with Hector. He asked her to come live with him in her dreams, which she welcomed, Rose to visit. Rose then got a call from The Corinthian, who passed the phone to Jed, who revealed that they were at the Royal Empire Hotel in Georgia.

The Corinthian and Jed entered the hotel for the serial killer convention, which Jed mistook for a cereal convention. At the counter, he was approached by [Nimrod](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Nimrod_(Netflix) "Nimrod (Netflix)") and [The Good Doctor](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/The_Good_Doctor "The Good Doctor"), who advised him to keep Jed away from the convention areas.

[![Image 4: Gilbert asking to join Rose](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sandman/images/b/bb/Netflix_The_Sandman_109_Collectors_02_Gilbert_Rose.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/250?cb=20220810163736)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sandman/images/b/bb/Netflix_The_Sandman_109_Collectors_02_Gilbert_Rose.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20220810163736)

Gilbert asking to join Rose

As Rose prepared to leave for her trip to pick up Jed, she received a visit from [Gilbert](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Gilbert_(Netflix) "Gilbert (Netflix)"), who informed her that Jed had been found and that she was on her way to get him in Georgia. Upon learning that she'd be going alone, Gilbert volunteered to join her on the trip.

While waiting for The Corinthian, Jed unknowingly met the acquaintance of [Fun Land](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Fun_Land "Fun Land"), a suspected pedophile, whom The Corinthian warned to leave Jed unharmed.

On the road to Georgia, Gilbert explained to Rose that when he left home, he made it his mission to see as much of the world as possible. To him, the object of travel was to set foot in one's own country as a foreign land.

[![Image 5: Hector and lyta following the earthquake](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sandman/images/3/3c/Netflix_The_Sandman_109_Collectors_09_Hector_Lyta.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/250?cb=20220810163752)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sandman/images/3/3c/Netflix_The_Sandman_109_Collectors_09_Hector_Lyta.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20220810163752)

Hector and lyta following the earthquake

Lyta returned to [the Dreaming](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/The_Dreaming "The Dreaming"), where she and Hector were having sex, until suddenly there was an earthquake that shook the house. It had never happened before, but beyond the momentary quake, everything appeared as it should.

In search of Lucienne, [Mervyn](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Mervyn_Pumpkinhead_(Netflix) "Mervyn Pumpkinhead (Netflix)") came across Dream, to whom he reported some minor seismic activity and damage. Dream's palace then began to shake and crack itself, though he assured Mervyn he would find the cause of the disturbance and eliminate it.

Dream returned some books to the library and took the opportunity to assess the damage from the recent disturbances. He asked if Lucienne had any idea what caused them, but she remained frustrated from their last encounter, in which he implied that her efforts beyond the library were without value, which was not his intent. Lucienne suspected that the vortex was the cause of the disturbances, though Dream argued that it could be something new.

Rose called [Unity](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Unity_Kinkaid_(Netflix) "Unity Kinkaid (Netflix)") to inform her that she was on the way to pick up Jed. Thrilled that everything was coming together, she offered to have them both flown out to her and have Mr. Holdaway look into making Rose, Jed's legal guardian.

Nervous because she hadn't seen him since he was five years old, Rose began to fear that Jed wouldn't like her or she wouldn't like him. She suspected that he was much different now.

After instructing Jed to stay in the room, The Corinthian made his way down to the conference room, where Nimrod took the stage to kick off the event, laying down the rules, from not using civilian names to no killing at the hotel, then introducing The Corinthian as their special guest of honor.

What fascinated Gilbert about humanity was that so many people were looking for reasons to be unhappy. Still, Rose didn't appear too interested in his take on the world, falling asleep in the car as he spoke of hope. In her dream, Rose came across Lyta, who expressed having been in the Dreaming for months despite it only being a couple of hours in the waking world. From afar, they were being watched by Dream and Matthew, who confirmed that Lucienne was right about the source of the disturbances.

Rose and Lyta returned to her home to find Dream awaiting their return, along with Hector, who revealed that Morpheus wanted them to leave because a ghost could not escape his fate by hiding in the Dreaming, nor could a living human being escape their grief there. Their presence had done much damage to the realm, and so Lyta and Hector had to part ways. Lyta refused to leave, exclaiming for Dream to leave, but instead, he returned Hector to his appointed place before informing Lyta that he would allow her to keep the baby for the time being, but it was conceived in the Dreaming, thus he had claiming rights, and one day, he would come for it. Morpheus then proceeded to end the dream, though he was followed back to his palace by Rose, the cause of all of this. Rose warned Dream against coming for her or her friends again. She suggested that he leave her alone before leaving the dream and awakening in the car, to a call from Lyta, who was emotionally distressed over Hector's loss.

The Corinthian was a bit of a celebrity among the other "collectors." But it was one man in particular who appeared to catch his attention, who claimed to be a collector known as "[The Boogieman](https://sandman.fandom.com/wiki/Philip_Sitz_(Netflix) "Philip Sitz (Netflix)")." However, Corinthian informed Nimrod and The Good Doctor that the man before them was not the Boogieman, who drowned three years ago in Louisiana. They were faced with an imposter. The Corinthian then caught sight of a child whom he believed to be Jed and followed him into the lobby.

[![Image 6: Rose and Gilbert arriving at the hotel](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sandman/images/9/96/Netflix_The_Sandman_109_Collectors_10_Gilbert_Rose.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/250?cb=20220810163754)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sandman/images/9/96/Netflix_The_Sandman_109_Collectors_10_Gilbert_Rose.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20220810163754)

Rose and Gilbert arriving at the hotel

Rose and Gilbert arrived at the hotel, where they were confronted by Fun Land, who informed them that the sectioned-off area of the hotel was for convention attendees only. Rather than turning away, Rose snatched a couple of attendee badges before slipping into the convention hall, where Gilbert realized they were at a serial killers convention.

Nimrod and The Good Doctor reconvened with The Corinthian after discovering that their Boogieman imposter was actually a fanboy named Philip Sitz. They collectively decided to "collect" Philip as a team. It was then that Corinthian met the gaze of Gilbert; the two locked eyes as if they were familiar.

Still posing as The Boogieman, Philip began conversing with some of the other collectors. Meanwhile, Gilbert left a message at the front desk for Rose before fleeing the hotel. Rose then approached the front desk in search of Jed, but instead, she learned that there was a room already registered in her name and a message from Gilbert, who had left and gone home.

Dream found Lucienne in the library, who admitted that she was right about the vortex being the source of the disturbances. He also admitted that he was wrong to hope that she would help them locate the missing Arcana. However, Lucienne revealed that he wasn't entirely wrong, as Rose did manage to find The Corinthian and Fiddler's Green, who, in actuality, was Gilbert, who returned to the Dreaming and apologized to Morpheus for having left. Without Dream, he was curious. Life as a human contained a substance that he never even imagined, which is why he returned, because The Corinthian was murdering them.

[![Image 7: Philip being confronted](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sandman/images/8/83/Netflix_The_Sandman_109_Collectors_04_The_Corinthian_Philip.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/250?cb=20220810163742)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sandman/images/8/83/Netflix_The_Sandman_109_Collectors_04_The_Corinthian_Philip.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20220810163742)

Philip being confronted

Rather than getting a drink at the bar as they had planned, The Corinthian led Philip into a secluded area of the hotel, where Nimrod and The Good Doctor confronted him. The three of them proceeded to kill Philip until being interrupted by Jed, who Corinthian pursued. Fleeing The Corinthian, Jed ran into Fun Land.

Gilbert learned from Lucienne that much like himself, Dream spent the last century in the waking realm. And while they may have had different experiences, Gilbert believed that his time there changed him, given Dream's apology to Lucienne, who was initially incapable of such a thing. If that were true, perhaps he would be merciful to Gilbert, since he came back in his own, Lucienne hoped. But Gilbert was only concerned with Dream stopping The Corinthian and saving Rose until Lucienne informed him that Rose was a vortex, meaning that Dream had to kill her.

[![Image 8: Fun Land chasing after Rose and Jed](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sandman/images/7/7c/Netflix_The_Sandman_109_Collectors_08_Fun_Land.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/250?cb=20220810163749)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sandman/images/7/7c/Netflix_The_Sandman_109_Collectors_08_Fun_Land.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20220810163749)

Fun Land chasing after Rose and Jed

While searching for the room registered to her name, Rose found Jed in the hallway with Fun Land, who was attempting to get Jed into his room. He then grabbed Jed by his jacket, refusing to let him go until Jed elbowed him and escaped with Rose, though Fun Land proceeded to chase after them and cornered them at the end of the hall, where he was then stabbed in the back and killed by The Corinthian.

Balance: Jimmy Essex and Charles on how they indulge while maintaining their healthy lifestyle
==============================================================================================

By [Gay Times](https://www.gaytimes.com/author/gaytimes/)

2nd October 2019

![Image 2: Two men smile in a close-up outdoor portrait, with one wearing a cap and nose ring and the other with a shaved head and a light green shirt](https://www.gaytimes.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/charles-jimmy-essex-celebroty-cruises.jpg)

#### What happens when you put eight leading LGBTQ creatives on a luxury cruise ship?

We found out when we followed some familiar faces onboard Celebrity Edge as they travelled around some of the Mediterranean’s most beautiful destinations this past summer.

As part of a new five-part series titled Trailblazers, the eight queer creatives set sail to key LGBTQ European destinations including Barcelona, Valencia, Ibiza, Nice, and Rome.

The series culminates in the third annual Pride at Sea onboard Celebrity Edge, featuring a guest interview from Adam Rippon.

Like us all, actor Jimmy Essex and musician Charles love to eat good food – especially when they are on holiday.

“At breakfast we plan what we’re going to have for lunch, and at lunch we plan what we’re going to have for dinner,” laughs Jimmy.

In this third episode, the couple indulge in the cuisine offered in the multiple restaurants available on Celebrity Edge, while balancing it out by using the gym facilities to maintain their healthy lifestyle.

![Image 3: Group of men and women holding a rainbow flag and an X-shaped symbol flag stand on the boat deck while pulling a rope](https://www.gaytimes.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/gay-times-celebrity-cruises-header.jpg)
The pair take in the breathtaking views around the ship as they do a lap (or five) on the ship’s running track.

Launching daily on GAY TIMES and Celebrity Cruises social media channels from 30 September until 4 October 2019, each mini-episode of Trailblazers paves the way for a perfect LGBTQ travel experience.

The cast includes: YouTuber and broadcaster**Riyadh Khalaf**and his partner**Josh Harrison**; presenter**Helen Scott**and life coach**Char Bailey**;**Jimmy Essex**and**Charlie Simmons**, a couple from the music and entertainment industry; and last but certainly not least, vogue dancer**, Jay Jay Revlon**and his best friend, podcast presenter**Lee Gray**.

Check out our[Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/gaytimes)for the daily episodes, which will launch at 7pm each evening.

**To book your dream getaway,**[**visit Celebrity Cruises here**](https://www.celebritycruises.co.uk/)**.**

Along with the [titular character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_/(character/) "Dream (character)") and [his siblings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endless_/(comics/) "Endless (comics)"), _[The Sandman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman_/(comic_book/) "The Sandman (comic book)")_ includes a large array of characters: inhabitants of the [Dreaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreaming_/(comics/) "Dreaming (comics)"), various deities, angels and demons, [faeries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faerie_/(DC_Comics/) "Faerie (DC Comics)"), immortals and witches. Some characters appear in _The Sandman_ (1989–1994), some in spinoffs like _[The Dreaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dreaming_/(comics/) "The Dreaming (comics)")_ (1996–2001) and _[Lucifer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucifer_/(DC_Comics/) "Lucifer (DC Comics)")_ (1999–2007), and others in earlier stories that _The Sandman_ was based on as well as the [podcast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman_/(podcast/) "The Sandman (podcast)") and the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") [TV series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman_/(TV_series/) "The Sandman (TV series)"). Their stories occur in the [DC Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Universe "DC Universe"), generally tangentially to the mainstream DC stories.

The **Endless** are a family of seven [anthropomorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropomorphism "Anthropomorphism") personifications of universal concepts, around whom much of the series revolves. They are the children of Mother **[Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyx "Nyx")** and Father **[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Father_Time "Father Time")**. All debuted in the _Sandman_ series, except Destiny, who was created by [Marv Wolfman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marv_Wolfman "Marv Wolfman") and [Berni Wrightson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berni_Wrightson "Berni Wrightson") in _[Weird Mystery Tales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weird_Mystery_Tales "Weird Mystery Tales")_ #1 (1972).[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#cite_note-1)

From eldest to youngest, they are:

**[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Father_Time "Father Time")** is the personification of time and the father of the Endless. He resides in the Realm of Time and was the one who gifted Destiny with his Cosmic Log.

In the Netflix series, Time is portrayed by [Rufus Sewell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rufus_Sewell "Rufus Sewell").

**[Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyx "Nyx")** is the personification of night and the mother of the Endless through Time.

In the Netflix series, Night is portrayed by [Tanya Moodie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanya_Moodie "Tanya Moodie").

Dreams and nightmares
---------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_Sandman_characters&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Dreams and nightmares")\]

These inhabitants of the [Dreaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dreaming_/(comics/) "The Dreaming (comics)") are often ordinary human beings who later became either dreams or nightmares.

**Cain** and **Abel** are based on the Biblical [Cain and Abel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cain_and_Abel "Cain and Abel"), adapted by editor [Joe Orlando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Orlando "Joe Orlando") with [Bob Haney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Haney "Bob Haney") (writer) and [Jack Sparling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Sparling "Jack Sparling") (artist) (Cain), and Mark Hannerfeld (writer) and [Bill Draut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Draut "Bill Draut") (artist) (Abel). They were depicted together in Abel's first appearance, and parted to their respective Houses at the end of the story. Although Cain would abuse Abel, he was not shown killing him until _Swamp Thing_ vol. 2 #33. In _[Elvira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassandra_Peterson "Cassandra Peterson")'s House of Mystery_ #11, Cain expresses shock at having killed his brother in recent times. In the same issue, a contest-winning letter establishes that Cain and the House exist both in the dream world and the real world, and that only in the dream world does Cain continue to harm Abel. In _The Sandman_, Cain is shown to kill Abel quite often. In issue #2, Lucien calls this unusual and recent.

Originally, they were the respective "hosts" of the [EC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EC_Comics "EC Comics")\-style [horror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_fiction "Horror fiction") [comic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_book "Comic book") anthologies _[House of Mystery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Mystery "House of Mystery")_ and _[House of Secrets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Secrets_/(DC_Comics/) "House of Secrets (DC Comics)")_ which ran from the 1950s through 1983—Cain debuting in _House of Mystery_ #175 (1968) and Abel in _DC Special_ #4 and _House of Secrets_ #81 (both 1969). During the 1970s, they also co-hosted the horror/humor anthology _[Plop!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plop! "Plop!")_. They were also both recurring characters in DC's _Elvira's House of Mystery_ (1986–1988).

In 1985, the characters were revived by writer [Alan Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Moore "Alan Moore"), who introduced them into his _[Swamp Thing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swamp_Thing "Swamp Thing")_ series in issue #33, retelling the Swamp Thing's original origin story from a 1971 issue of _House of Secrets_. [Gary Cohn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Cohn_/(comics/) "Gary Cohn (comics)") and [Dan Mishkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Mishkin "Dan Mishkin") included them in the pages of _[Blue Devil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Devil_/(DC_Comics/) "Blue Devil (DC Comics)")_ in 1986. [Jamie Delano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Delano "Jamie Delano") also occasionally used them in a [cameo role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameo_role "Cameo role") in his title _[Hellblazer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellblazer "Hellblazer")_.

In Gaiman's _Sandman_ universe, the biblical [Cain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cain "Cain") and [Abel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel "Abel") live in the Dreaming at Dream's invitation. This is based on the verse in the Bible which says that Cain was sent to live in the [Land of Nod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_of_Nod "Land of Nod"). They live as neighbors in two houses near a graveyard: Cain in the broad [House of Mystery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Mystery "House of Mystery") and Abel in the tall [House of Secrets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Secrets_/(DC_Comics/) "House of Secrets (DC Comics)"). According to their appearance in _Swamp Thing_, the difference is that 'a mystery may be shared, but a secret must be forgotten if one tries to tell it'.

Gaiman's Cain is an aggressive, overbearing character. He is a thin, long-limbed man with an angular, drawn face, glasses, a tufty beard, and hair drawn into two points above his ears. He has been described by other characters as sounding "just like [Vincent Price](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Price "Vincent Price")".[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#cite_note-2)

Gaiman's Abel is a nervous but kind-hearted man. He also has a stammer. He is somewhat similar in appearance to Cain, with a tufty beard and hair that comes to points above his ears, though his hair is black rather than brown. He is shorter and fatter than Cain, with a more open face. It is eventually learned that the only time he does not stutter is when he is telling a story or when he is dead.

Cain kills Abel frequently and in many brutal ways, whereupon Abel later returns to life. He often expresses hope for a more harmonious relationship with his brother.

Cain and Abel own a large green draconic [gargoyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gargoyle "Gargoyle") named [Gregory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#Gregory), who also made his debut in _House of Mystery_ #175. In the first appearance of the characters in _Sandman_, issue #2, Cain gives Abel an egg that soon hatches into another gargoyle, a small golden one. Abel names the gargoyle "Irving". but Cain insists that the names of gargoyles must always begin with a "G.", and Abel (after another death and resurrection) renames the gargoyle "[Goldie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#Goldie)", after an invisible/imaginary friend to whom Abel told his early _House of Secrets_ stories. A letter in issue #91 was attributed to Goldie, who claimed that it was herself depicted on the cover of issue #88.

They shelter Dream until his strength is restored following his 72-year-long imprisonment. In the fourth [story arc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Story_arc "Story arc"), _[Season of Mists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman:_Season_of_Mists "The Sandman: Season of Mists")_, Cain is sent to [Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hell "Hell") to give a message to [Lucifer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucifer_/(DC_Comics/) "Lucifer (DC Comics)") because Cain is protected by [a curse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curse_and_mark_of_Cain "Curse and mark of Cain") that would deter Lucifer from harming him. Cain and Abel also aid [The Corinthian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#The_Corinthian) with the child [Daniel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Hall_/(comics/) "Daniel Hall (comics)") during _[The Kindly Ones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman:_The_Kindly_Ones "The Sandman: The Kindly Ones")_, the penultimate story arc of the series. Abel is one of the victims of the [Furies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#The_Three) in this series and is brought back to life by the new [Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Hall_/(comics/) "Daniel Hall (comics)") at Cain's request.

In the podcast, Cain and Abel are voiced by Michael Roberts and [Kerry Shale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerry_Shale "Kerry Shale").

In the Netflix series _[The Sandman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman_/(TV_series/) "The Sandman (TV series)")_, Cain and Abel are portrayed by [Sanjeev Bhaskar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjeev_Bhaskar "Sanjeev Bhaskar") and [Asim Chaudhry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asim_Chaudhry "Asim Chaudhry") respectively.

**The Corinthian** is a nightmare created by Dream, of human appearance but with two small additional mouths in place of his eyes. He enjoys eating the eyeballs of people he kills.

The first version of the Corinthian is destroyed by Dream while speaking at a "Cereal Convention" for spending several unsupervised decades on Earth as a serial killer (in Dream's view, a waste of his potential), and it is shown in _[The Sandman: Overture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman:_Overture "The Sandman: Overture")_ (2013) that Dream intended to do this before his imprisonment.

Near the end of the series, Dream creates a second Corinthian, altering his personality to be obedient and useful rather than homicidal. In a later story in _The Dreaming_, the second Corinthian is haunted by the actions of the first.

In the [podcast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman_/(podcast/) "The Sandman (podcast)"), the Corinthian is voiced by [Riz Ahmed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riz_Ahmed "Riz Ahmed").

The Corinthian is portrayed by [Boyd Holbrook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boyd_Holbrook "Boyd Holbrook") in the Netflix series, having a more expanded role before the Doll's House arc. He is shown to manipulate circumstances regarding Ethel Cripps' death and behaves in a much less hostile way to Jed Walker, appearing to not desire to harm him. He is also shown as gay or pansexual in the series, often having sex with his male victims before killing them.

**Eve** is a special character who has been seen in the _Lucifer_ series and is depicted as living in a cave in The Dreaming.

**[Fiddler's Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiddler%27s_Green "Fiddler's Green")** is the personification of a place in the Dreaming which all travelers (specifically sailors) dream of someday finding. It sometimes assumes human form and goes wandering under the alias **Gilbert**, a kindly, portly man who resembles [G. K. Chesterton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G._K._Chesterton "G. K. Chesterton") (the G stood for Gilbert) in appearance and behavior. As "Gilbert", Fiddler's Green accompanied [Rose Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#Rose_Walker) to find her brother Jed and gave her the means by which to summon Dream to rescue her from danger at the Cereal Convention that the Corinthian was speaking at. Afterwards, Fiddler's Green thereafter returned to the Dreaming and resumed his true form before Rose. He was killed by the Three in _[The Kindly Ones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman:_The_Kindly_Ones "The Sandman: The Kindly Ones")_ and refused to be resurrected by the [new Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Hall_/(comics/) "Daniel Hall (comics)") as his death will have no meaning. Dream allows Fiddler's Green to return to the dead.

In the podcast, Fiddler's Green is voiced by [Ray Porter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Porter "Ray Porter").

In the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") series, Fiddler's Green is portrayed by [Stephen Fry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Fry "Stephen Fry"). This version of Gilbert has a slightly smaller role than in the comics, but still accompanies Rose to the Cereal Convention (under the name of "Dutch Uncle", the name of an unseen serial killer in that issue whose name was seen on a piece of paper). Following Corinthian's defeat, Fiddler's Green returns to his true form upon returning to the Dreaming.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#cite_note-SlashFilm:_CastExpands-4)

A [Wyvern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyvern "Wyvern"), a [Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Griffin "Griffin"), and a [Hippogriff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hippogriff "Hippogriff") are the **[gate keepers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gatekeeper "Gatekeeper")** of Dream's castle and are also referred to as the **Guardians of the Gate**. The wyvern was more land dragon-like and had no dragon wings until later appearances, the griffin also had a lion mane and has all four legs of a lion, and the hippogriff was depicted with a [winged horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winged_horse "Winged horse")\-like appearance. The gate keepers often intercept anyone from entering Dream's Ghost Castle. They derive all their power and authority from Dream so when Dream was captured and lost his power, they could no longer guard or protect the Dreaming.

Their first comic book appearance was in "Dream of a Thousand Cats" where the Siamese Cat had to get past them in order to see the Cat of Dreams.

In issue #24, the Guardians of the Gate see a lot of envoys showing up at the Ghost Castle in light of Lucifer's abdication. The Griffin sends a message through his statue in the throne room to inform Dream about it and that the Guardians of the Gate can't keep them all back. Dream instructs the Griffin to tell his fellow Guardians of the Gate to let them in.

Delirium later runs into the Guardians of the Gate where she is briefly picked up by the Wyvern when she tried to enter Dream's castle.

After the Griffin was destroyed by the Three in their Erinyes aspect, the new Dream did not recreate him. Instead, he asked the Gryphons of Greek myth to send one of their own. The Queen of Gryphons dispatches a Gryphon of Arimapsa to replace the Dreaming's Griffin. When Matthew meets this Gryphon (who is depicted with cattle-like hooves for back legs) and informs him of being the only Griffin of his land to meet the new Dream's requirements, he informs Matthew that his land of Arimapsa is somewhere far from the Dreaming. The Guardians of the Gate state to Matthew that they have been sent by the new Dream to attend Dream's wake, but opted not to leave their post. (_The Sandman_ Vol. 2 #71)

In the podcast, the Wyvern, the Griffin, and the Hippogriff are voiced by Harry Myers, [Ray Porter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Porter "Ray Porter"), and [Tom Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Alexander_/(actor/) "Tom Alexander (actor)").

In the Netflix series, the Wyvern, the Griffin, and the Hippogriff are shown on the castle with the Wyvern voiced by [Nonso Anozie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonso_Anozie "Nonso Anozie"), the Griffin voiced by [Diane Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_Morgan "Diane Morgan") in season one and by [Jo Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin "Jo Martin") in season two, and the Hippogriff voiced by [Tom Wu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Wu "Tom Wu") in season one and by [Paul Rhys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Rhys "Paul Rhys") in season two. The Wyvern resembled his mythological depiction and the Griffin is a female. Their roles in the animated episode "Dream of a Thousand Cats", the confrontation of the envoys, and Delirium's encounter with them remain intact. Unlike the comics, the Kindly Ones' Erinyes aspect tried to kill the Griffin by aging her bones only for Dream to come out and heal her.

**Gregory** is the pet [gargoyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gargoyle "Gargoyle") of [Cain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cain_and_Abel_/(comics/) "Cain and Abel (comics)").

Gregory appears in the Netflix series. He was willingly absorbed by Dream in order to help restore the Dreaming prior to Dream's quest to reclaim his stolen items.

**Goldie** is a fictional character in _[The Sandman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman_/(Vertigo/) "The Sandman (Vertigo)")_ [comic book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_book "Comic book") series by [Neil Gaiman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Gaiman "Neil Gaiman").

Goldie is a pet baby [gargoyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gargoyle "Gargoyle"), given to [Abel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cain_and_Abel_/(comics/) "Cain and Abel (comics)") by his brother [Cain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cain_and_Abel_/(comics/) "Cain and Abel (comics)") in _[Preludes and Nocturnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman:_Preludes_and_Nocturnes "The Sandman: Preludes and Nocturnes")_. Abel originally intends to name him Irving, but Cain insists that gargoyle names must all begin with a "G". Cain then proceeded to murder Abel over this. Abel soon returns as he is murdered by Cain all the time. He then agrees to name the gargoyle Goldie, after "an old friend", though he tells Goldie in private that he will continue to think of him as Irving.

Goldie appears for a short scene in _[The Doll's House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman:_The_Doll%27s_House "The Sandman: The Doll's House")_ in which he is sitting upon Abel's shoulder as Lucien asks Abel about the inhabitants of the house. He later appears throughout the "Parliament of Rooks" story in _[Fables and Reflections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman:_Fables_and_Reflections "The Sandman: Fables and Reflections")_, and briefly at the beginning of _[Brief Lives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman:_Brief_Lives "The Sandman: Brief Lives")_. He also accompanies Abel in _[The Kindly Ones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman:_The_Kindly_Ones "The Sandman: The Kindly Ones")_ and is with him when he gets murdered by the Furies, crying when his master is killed. He is later seen playing with [Daniel Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Hall_/(comics/) "Daniel Hall (comics)").

Goldie later takes on a pivotal role as the guardian of the tree of life in the _Sandman_ spin-off series _[The Dreaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dreaming_/(comics/) "The Dreaming (comics)")_. On his/her quest to the tree, a search party forms. He was retconned into a female gargoyle for the new series.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#cite_note-vert-drea-5)

Goldie is named after the "'imaginary' friend" to whom Abel would tell his early stories in the pages of _[House of Secrets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Secrets_/(DC_Comics/) "House of Secrets (DC Comics)")_.

In issue 39 of the 2008 reboot of the _[House of Mystery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Mystery_/(Vertigo/) "House of Mystery (Vertigo)")_ comic series, it is revealed that Goldie is "Gigi", a waitress at the House of Mystery and a bit player in the series. Goldie was transformed by Lotus Blossom, another character in the series, at Goldie's request in exchange for a book of magic spells. Goldie was not enthralled with the idea of growing up to be a gargoyle, and instead wanted to be a human girl. The newly reborn Gigi joined Lotus Blossom on her exploits in the series, often serving as an enforcer for her. It is revealed that Abel knows Gigi's true history, but if his brother Cain knew, it was not shown.

In the podcast, Goldie's vocal effects were provided by Karen Batke.

Goldie appears in the Netflix series.

**Lucien** is the chief [librarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Librarian "Librarian") in the Dreaming, and is a tall thin, bookish man. He first appeared in _[Weird Mystery Tales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weird_Mystery_Tales "Weird Mystery Tales")_ #18 (May 1975) and was apparently killed in _[Secrets of Haunted House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secrets_of_Haunted_House "Secrets of Haunted House")_ #44 (January 1982).[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#cite_note-dc-ency-6)

Like [Cain and Abel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#Cain_and_Abel), Lucien, created by [Paul Levitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Levitz "Paul Levitz"), [Nestor Redondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nestor_Redondo "Nestor Redondo"), and [Joe Orlando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Orlando "Joe Orlando"), was originally the host of a 1970s "weird tales" comic, specifically the three-issue _[Tales of Ghost Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tales_of_Ghost_Castle "Tales of Ghost Castle")_ (May/June–October 1975). In that series, he is portrayed as the guardian of a castle in [Transylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transylvania "Transylvania") abandoned by both sides during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"),[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#cite_note-7)\[_[full citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources#What_information_to_include "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_\] watching over its forgotten library with his companion, a [werewolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Werewolf "Werewolf") named Rover. In his first appearance in _[Preludes and Nocturnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman:_Preludes_and_Nocturnes "The Sandman: Preludes and Nocturnes")_ (issue #2) this is [retroactively](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retcon "Retcon") revealed to be Dream's castle.

Lucien is the effective keeper of the Dreaming in Dream's absence, and becomes one of Dream's most faithful and trusted servants after proving his loyalty by never abandoning his post during that period. His primary function is to protect the Library, wherein are contained all the books that have ever been dreamed of, including the ones that have never been written. The titles of some of these books, many of which are sequels to real works, are visible. He is, despite his frail appearance, apparently quite capable in combat, "\[dealing\] with" several unpleasant creatures who escape imprisonment during the events of _The Kindly Ones_.

In issue #68, it is revealed that Lucien's existence in the Dreaming began as serving the role of Dream's first [raven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raven "Raven"). When writing _[The Sandman Companion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman_Companion "The Sandman Companion")_, author Hy Bender interpreted this as meaning that Lucien was also [the first man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam "Adam"). An allusion to "Mr. Raven", the ghostly librarian in [George MacDonald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_MacDonald "George MacDonald")'s novel _[Lilith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lilith_/(novel/) "Lilith (novel)")_, may be intended.

In the podcast, Lucien is voiced by [Simon Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Vance "Simon Vance").

In the Netflix series, [Vivienne Acheampong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivienne_Acheampong "Vivienne Acheampong") portrays Lucienne, a gender-swapped version of Lucien.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#cite_note-Ramos-8)

**Matthew** is the [raven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raven "Raven") companion of Dream.

Matthew was originally Matthew Cable, a long-time supporting character in the _[Swamp Thing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swamp_Thing "Swamp Thing")_ series, but because he died while asleep in the Dreaming, he was offered the chance to become a dream raven and serve Dream if he wished, and he accepted.

Matthew is not the first of Morpheus' ravens. Former ravens include [Aristeas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aristeas "Aristeas") of [Marmora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marmara_Island "Marmara Island"), who returned to his life as a man for one year at one point, and [Lucien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Sandman_characters#Lucien), the first of the ravens. Morpheus seems to keep the ravens around out of some sort of unspoken need for companionship, though he also sends them on occasional missions.

Matthew's [word balloons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_balloon "Speech balloon") and [font style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letterer "Letterer") are scratchy and uneven, probably to represent a hoarse, cawing voice, and perhaps as an indicator of his crude, smart-aleck personality. Underneath his frequently irreverent manner, Matthew is actually very loyal to Dream, and he is one of the characters who takes it the hardest when Dream perishes, initially seeking release from his service, but eventually coming to terms with his loss and choosing to remain as [Daniel Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Hall_/(comics/) "Daniel Hall (comics)")'s raven after speaking to different characters.
